articles.title: Will Kawhi Leonard have his jersey retired? Toronto embraces the most unique legacy in the NBA
articles.summary: As Leonard kicks off his second tenure with Toronto, do the Raptors represent his best shot at having his jersey retired?
articles.body:
As we tip off the 2026-27 season, I don't begrudge NBA fans who are desperately trying to make sense of this past offseason. We are right there with you. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown are Sixers? Giannis Antetokounmpo is in South Beach? The Washington Wizards gave Trae Young how much ?

The biggest plot twist, however, involves our friends north of the border. In the aftermath of the stiffest punishment in NBA history handed down by commissioner Adam Silver on LA Clippers owner Steve Ballmer and his eternally beleaguered franchise, Kawhi Leonard has largely escaped unscathed. And not only that, Leonard, the grand prize of the Clippers' cap circumvention, has returned to the team that originally flagged cap circumvention shadiness to the league office when he left — the Toronto Raptors.

Yes, Kawhi Leonard is a Raptor, picking up where he left off in 2019 in a quest to bring another title to Canada. He continues what is the most confusing NBA legacy of his generation. A two-time Finals MVP, seven-time All-NBA selection and two-time Defensive Player of the Year who, as of now, is no lock to have his jersey retired by any of his former teams.

It's a question that I can't stop thinking about as NBA fans wrestle with how one of the game's greats will be remembered following a historic cap scandal: Do the Raptors represent Leonard's best shot at having his jersey retired?

In the player empowerment era, the fascinating case of Leonard could help shape the legacies of his superstar peers who jump from team to team.

Imagine telling an NBA fan in 2017 how this Kawhi Leonard story would play out. At the time, Leonard had earned back-to-back Defensive Player of the Year awards, had already won a championship and a Finals MVP. The Spurs were coming off back-to-back 60-win seasons, and Leonard was the face of it all.

If you look up in the rafters at the Spurs' arena, you'll see Timmy, Tony and Manu's jerseys up there. And for a while, it seemed like Leonard's No. 2 jersey would be right next to them.

But things in San Antonio soured quickly. After some disagreements about how the team handled his knee injury, Kawhi's magical rise with the Spurs had a sudden and bitter downfall. Leonard played just nine games in the 2017-18 season and, in the summer of 2018, the Spurs traded Kawhi and Danny Green to the Raptors for DeMar DeRozan, Jakob Poeltl and a top-20 protected 2019 first-round draft pick.

Spurs fans weren't happy with how it all went down. Every time Leonard played in San Antonio, boos rained down from every corner of the arena. But Gregg Popovich, Leonard's longtime coach, was not pleased with it. In a November matchup in 2023 against Leonard's Clippers, Popovich took the PA announcer's microphone in the middle of Leonard's trip to the free-throw line and demanded an end to the booing.

"Excuse me for a second," Popovich said. "Can we stop all the booing and let these guys play? Have a little class. That's not who we are. Knock off the booing."

Coach Pop's backing was unusual, but it did reveal a continued heartfelt connection with his former Finals MVP who left on uneasy terms. Leonard's reception in San Antonio may still be icy, but if history is a guide, the team will honor him one day with a jersey retirement.

And so will the Raptors. Even if he played just one season in Toronto.

In January, the Raptors will hold a ceremony to retire Kyle Lowry's No. 7 jersey alongside Vince Carter's No. 15 in the Toronto rafters.

Lowry's case is a no-brainer. He appeared in 409 Raptors wins, making him the winningest player in franchise history. He is also the franchise leader in assists, steals, made 3s, triple-doubles and All-Star appearances. And for that, just a few weeks ago, the Raptors unveiled their Kyle Lowry statue, which is comically not Lowry at all, but a dinosaur with a basketball jersey on.

Though it may seem controversial now, it seems likely that Kawhi Leonard's No. 2 jersey will join No. 7 and No. 15 one day.

Based on one standard, there's no question that Leonard will have his jersey retired by the Raptors.

I researched every Finals MVP winner in NBA history and looked to see if the franchise had retired his jersey. And here are the facts: There have been 28 Finals MVPs who are no longer playing in the NBA. All 28 of them have seen their jerseys rise up to the rafters of their respective buildings.

That list of Finals MVPs includes Cedric Maxwell of the Boston Celtics and Andre Iguodala of the Golden State Warriors. They are the only Finals MVPs who have had their jersey retired but have not been inducted into the Hall of Fame. And they help set a precedent for Leonard, who won Finals MVP in both San Antonio and Toronto.

But here's the thing: Maxwell and Iguodala each logged eight seasons with their Finals MVP teams. If it weren't for this trade back to Toronto, Leonard would be the shortest-tenured Finals MVP in league history. A one-and-done mercenary of this magnitude had never been seen before. Besides Kawhi, no player had ever left his team immediately after winning the Finals MVP. (That is, if you exclude Michael Jordan's two retirements with the Bulls.)

According to my research — which, I should note, excludes memorial jersey retirements like Reggie Lewis in Boston and Bobby Phills in Charlotte — Leonard would become one of four honored players who played fewer than four seasons with a team. Another caveat, this list does not count those who were players and coaches for their club, like Lenny Wilkens and Nate McMillan in Seattle, who muddy up the picture.

SHORTEST NUMBER OF SEASONS FOR RETIRED JERSEY

Jordan had his No. 23 retired by the Miami Heat in 2003 when legendary coach and exec Pat Riley decided to pay tribute to MJ. It is the one instance of an NBA team retiring a jersey of a player who's played less than a season with their club. (Did you ever wonder why LeBron James wore No. 6 and not No. 23 in Miami?) Nate Thurmond had his No. 42 jersey retired by the Cleveland Cavaliers despite playing in just one and a half seasons with the team and averaging a measly five points per game as the backup center. Look up "The Miracle of Richfield" sometime and you'll begin to understand Thurmond's legacy in Northeast Ohio. Not to mention the future Hall of Famer was from Akron, Ohio.

Kawhi is under contract for three more seasons, thanks to a contract extension signed this offseason. He can opt out after two seasons, which would bring his total seasons in Toronto to three. Even if Kawhi plays just three seasons in Toronto, it wouldn't be the shortest tenure.

Julius Erving had his jersey retired by the 76ers, but also by the Nets. In just three seasons with New York, Dr. J led the Nets to two championships and won three MVPs in the ABA.

Let's say Kawhi picks up his player option for the 2028-29 and finishes out his career with the Raptors after four seasons. How exclusive is the Four Seasons club? There are nine players who have had their jerseys retired with just four seasons in uniform. Shaq has done it twice.

The underlying throughline for most of these guys is relevant to Kawhi — seven of the 10 instances were driven by a championship run.

Given that every retired Finals MVP has had his jersey honored by his team and the fact that there have been several instances of retired jerseys for players with short tenures with their clubs, Kawhi can expect to see No. 2 join No. 7 and No. 15 one day in Toronto.

NBA superstars will be watching how the Raptors handle Leonard's situation.

In the player empowerment era headlined by LeBron James, it's common for the modern NBA superstar to switch teams in his prime, leaving various franchises with some tough decisions about jersey immortality.

Kevin Durant, for example, will have a fascinating case ahead of him. Will the No. 35 be retired in OKC? One hint is that, a year after KD left, PJ Dozier was allowed to wear No. 35 for OKC in 2017-18.

"Honestly I didn't even think twice about [Durant having it] ... I just saw it was open and took advantage of it."

The Thunder could still decide to honor Durant one day, and I suspect they will. His jersey could be retired by the Golden State Warriors as well, even though he played only three seasons there. He won two titles (and two Finals MVPs) in the Bay like Dr. J in New York. Elsewhere, Brooklyn, Phoenix and Houston would have less pressure to do so, considering he didn't reach past the second round in any of those three stops. Yet.

In the non-Finals-MVP department, Anthony Davis should also be curious about Kawhi. Davis left New Orleans on icy terms and, like Kawhi, won a title in his first season with his new club, the Lakers. Davis played longer in LA than Kawhi did in Toronto, but the Lakers may be a little pickier considering they have so many numbers retired as is.

Jimmy Butler is another superstar with a chance of retiring without being honored by a team. The six-time All-Star and five-time All-NBA standout has made a lasting impact in Chicago and Miami, but enough to be honored with a jersey retirement?

Chris Paul has strong cases in New Orleans and Los Angeles, but the latter franchise has seemingly sent the wrong messages. The Clippers already gave Paul's No. 3 to Bradley Beal this summer, months after they waived Paul unceremoniously in the middle of his farewell tour. It seems ludicrous that LA wouldn't honor Lob City with jersey retirements for Paul, Blake Griffin and DeAndre Jordan. But according to Griffin , he isn't exactly holding his breath on having his jersey retired by the Clippers.

But the guy who might be watching Kawhi's legacy closest? How about Paul George?

When they joined forces in 2019, it marked the biggest free-agency coup in franchise history and both seemed destined to be honored by the Clippers one day. Now, after the Kawhi scandal has tarnished his tenure with the team and considering George's association with that era, it's not looking too good that either of them will have their jerseys retired in the Intuit Dome.

Which leads us to this unbelievable fact. The Clippers are the only NBA team to not have any retired numbers in their 57-year history. Not from their San Diego days or the Buffalo Braves days. Zero jerseys hang in the Intuit rafters. Every retired Finals MVP has had his jersey raised to the rafters by his respective team, but not every MVP, as it turns out. The Clippers, who came from San Diego after the Buffalo Braves relocated, have not retired Bob McAdoo's jersey despite him winning the MVP award in 1975 with the Braves. It's a shame the Clippers should correct soon.

That's maybe the most twisted thing about this entire Kawhi Leonard jersey retirement story. He was the Clippers' best chance at having their first jersey up in the rafters. But now? Good luck getting that past Adam Silver.

The Clippers keep circumventing their own chances at having a jersey retirement ceremony one day. But as Leonard kicks off his second tenure with Toronto, he's all but certain to have his jersey retired by the Raptors. A second championship would remove all doubt.

articles.title: Kristaps Porzingis Trade Rumors Addressed by Warriors amid NBA Retirement Buzz
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors have "started exploring trade routes" involving veteran center Kristaps Porziņģis, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors have "started exploring trade routes" involving veteran center Kristaps Porziņģis, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Charania added that Porziņģis is "seriously contemplating his future in basketball" due to lingering effects from his postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome .

Every NBA Team's Top 3 Trade Targets This Season 🎯

In a statement , the Warriors said they "are not going to comment on trade speculation or reports regarding his health-related matter or future."

The Athletic's Sam Amick reported Wednesday that the Warriors contacted the Milwaukee Bucks about a potential trade for Porziņģis. However, the Bucks "are not believed to have any interest" in the veteran.

The 31-year-old is effectively on an expiring contract . He's making $20 million for the 2026-27 season and only $3 million of his $20 million payout in 2027-28 is guaranteed.

That's going to aid Golden State's efforts to move a player who might be done altogether in the league. His contract could give a team some added flexibility next summer in free agency.

The Warriors have draft assets that can sweeten the deal, too. Depending on how far into the future they're willing to go, one of their first-rounders could be very valuable when we're inching toward a post-Stephen Curry era.

Porziņģis averaged 16.1 points and 5.3 rebounds following his midseason trade to Golden State. His three-point shooting (31.1 percent) left something to be desired, though.

The front office and coaching staff will have had high expectations for the 2017-18 All-Star. His skill set matched nicely with the roster, and he had a full offseason to grow more accustomed to his surroundings.

Instead, ESPN's Anthony Slater reported that "team sources describe a detached Porziņģis as indifferent and uninterested in participating in scrimmages and strenuous on-court prep work" at a session arranged by Jimmy Butler last month.

Porziņģis proceeded to take an indefinite leave of absence.

Especially when Butler is such a wild card coming off a torn ACL, the Warriors can't afford to get nothing on the court from a $20 million salary slot.

With all of the factors at play, it's doubtful Golden State can flip Porziņģis for a major difference-maker unless general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. is willing to give up multiple first-round picks. Dunleavy might at least be able to land somebody who can slot into the frontcourt and be a close facsimile to the Latvian big.

articles.title: Ja Morant's Role in Blazers' Lineup Reportedly Revealed For Debut With Damian Lillard
articles.summary: Ja Morant will start next to Damian Lillard in the Portland Trail Blazers' backcourt to open the 2026-27 season, according to NBA insider Chris Haynes.
articles.body:
Ja Morant will start next to Damian Lillard in the Portland Trail Blazers' backcourt to open the 2026-27 season, according to NBA insider Chris Haynes .

Guards Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson are set to come off the bench for Portland assuming Toumani Camara, Deni Avdija and Donovan Clingan will occupy the team's remaining three starting spots.

The Trail Blazers acquired Morant in exchange for forwards Jerami Grant and Kris Murray in a trade with the Memphis Grizzlies on June 29.

NBA Stars with Most on the Line This Season 🫡

There was some uncertainty surrounding Portland's starting backcourt heading into training camp, as Holiday started 51 games last season while Lillard was sidelined due to his recovery from a torn Achilles .

Henderson only made 30 regular-season appearances, but thrived as a starter in the Trail Blazers' first-round playoff series against the San Antonio Spurs. The No. 3 overall pick in the 2023 NBA draft averaged 15.0 points per game on 47.5/46.4/75.0 shooting splits in the postseason.

Meanwhile, Morant started in 325 of his 327 games played throughout his seven-year tenure in Memphis.

The two-time All-Star was willing to accept a bench role following the change of scenery, though.

"I think winning is the most important thing for me," Morant told reporters on Sept. 28. "So whatever role I have to play to get that done, I don't think anybody would be mad after a win. As a starter, if I'm starting, if I'm not, it's the same thing. It's day one right now, I feel like that's coach's questions, but for me I have no problem with either."

The 27-year-old quickly blossomed into one of the league's top young point guards after the Grizzlies selected him with the No. 2 choice in the 2019 draft, but his time with the organization didn't end on a high note.

Morant recorded just 19.5 points per game last season, representing his lowest average since his 2020-21 campaign. He also shot a career-low 41.0 percent from the field and 23.5 percent from behind the arc.

An elbow injury limited him to 20 appearances.

It's worth noting that Morant started to look like his former self in the preseason with the Trail Blazers, averaging 11.5 points, 4.8 assists and 1.8 steals in 20.8 minutes per game. He connected on 56.7 percent of his field goals as well.

Portland will open the regular season against the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday night. Tip off is at 10 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Luka Dončić takes out full-page ad in LA Times ahead of Lakers season-opener vs. Warriors: 'We have a special team'
articles.summary: Dončić is heading into his second full season with L.A.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers open the 2026-27 season at home on Wednesday night against the Golden State Warriors.

Ahead of the game, star guard Luka Dončić took out a full-page ad in the LA Times and wrote a message to the Lakers faithful.

"Tonight we start our run for a championship. Every player dreams of holding that trophy. To do it for all you amazing fans would mean everything to us. Each of us understands what it means to put on this purple and gold jersey and follow the players who wore it before us. It means so much because of the passion and dedication that generations of you all have shown for this team. I see it everywhere. The hats, the flags on cars, the murals. This city has people from all over the world, speaking every language, and the Lakers are the thing that brings everyone together. We have a special team. We know what you expect, and we are going to do everything in our power to deliver it. From the moment I arrived in L.A., you welcomed me with open arms. That is something I will never forget. So here is my promise to you: we are going to give you everything we have, every single night. No excuses. No nights off. But we cannot do this alone. You are the best fans in the world, and we are going to need you. Every game, bring it with us. Let's go. "

"Tonight we start our run for a championship.

Every player dreams of holding that trophy. To do it for all you amazing fans would mean everything to us. Each of us understands what it means to put on this purple and gold jersey and follow the players who wore it before us. It means so much because of the passion and dedication that generations of you all have shown for this team.

I see it everywhere. The hats, the flags on cars, the murals. This city has people from all over the world, speaking every language, and the Lakers are the thing that brings everyone together.

We have a special team. We know what you expect, and we are going to do everything in our power to deliver it. From the moment I arrived in L.A., you welcomed me with open arms. That is something I will never forget.

So here is my promise to you: we are going to give you everything we have, every single night. No excuses. No nights off.

But we cannot do this alone. You are the best fans in the world, and we are going to need you. Every game, bring it with us.

Dončić is heading into his second full season with Los Angeles. He joined the Lakers ahead of the 2025 trade deadline in the infamous deal that sent him from the Dallas Mavericks to the Lakers overnight.

Last year, Dončić played 64 games for the Lakers, the most in a season since 2023-24. He averaged 33.5 points, 7.7 rebounds and 8.3 assists per game. It was the second-highest points-per-game mark of his career.

This marks a new era for Los Angeles, with Dončić as the team's focal point. It will be the first season since 2018 that the Lakers won't have LeBron James on the roster, as the future Hall of Famer signed with the Philadelphia 76ers in free agency this offseason.

Dončić's statement shows he knows his role now and what fans still expect from the franchise, even without James in town. The guard's first chance to back up his words comes in Wednesday night's season opener.

articles.title: Cavs' Donovan Mitchell Doesn't 'Ever Want to Wear Another Uniform,' Says He 'Can't Ever Picture It'
articles.summary: Cleveland Cavaliers star guard Donovan Mitchell has endeared himself to the Midwest, and he wants to stay put for the rest of his career.
articles.body:
Cleveland Cavaliers star guard Donovan Mitchell has endeared himself to the Midwest, and he wants to stay put for the rest of his career.

Mitchell told Chris Fedor of Cleveland.com that he signed his record-breaking four-year, $273 million extension with the Cavs this past summer because he wants to retire with the franchise.

"Everybody always says, 'Why Cleveland? Why Cleveland?' Cleveland's home," Mitchell said (h/t HoopsHype ). "I don't ever want to wear another uniform. I don't have that vision. Business is business. I understand how that works. There may be a situation where we may not be in a position to win anymore and business happens, right? … But the purpose behind this extension is to be here forever. … I've got to deliver. We've got to deliver. I'm not saying an extension guarantees a championship. But that's the goal. It's why I wake up every morning. I don't want to be anywhere else. I don't see it. Can't ever picture it. I dream of myself being here forever and hopefully having 45 in the rafters one day."

The 10 Biggest Contract Extensions in NBA History 💸

Mitchell's extension keeps him in Cleveland through the 2030–31 season and set a new record for average annual salary at $68 million. The Cavs acquired the 30-year-old from the Utah Jazz in 2022, and he's remained one of the top guards in the league with seven consecutive All-Star selections.

If Mitchell had waited until next offseason to sign an extension, he would've been eligible for a deal worth $353 million over five years. However, he told Fedor that he didn't want to wait or negotiate for more money, as he signed his current deal on the first day he became eligible on July 7.

"None of my feelings have changed," Mitchell said. "That, to me, is the sign of consistency on the court. It's the sign of consistency in the organization. For an organization that says, 'Hey, we're going to do X, Y, and Z,' and four years later, I'm sitting here and I'm looking back like, man, they did say this was going to happen, this was going to be a certain way and they delivered on everything and vice-versa."

Mitchell is motivated to lead the Cavs to an NBA championship, and the team will get started on that quest when it opens the 2026-27 season on Thursday against the Philadelphia 76ers.

articles.title: El San Pablo Burgos se desinfla tras el descanso y cae ante el Tortona (89-79)
articles.standfirst: El parcial de 31-17 recibido en el último cuarto terminó de hundir a los burgaleses
articles.summary: El parcial de 31-17 recibido en el último cuarto terminó de hundir a los burgaleses
articles.body: El Recoletas Salud San Pablo Burgos cayó derrotado por 89-79 ante el Derthona Tortona en un encuentro que tuvo controlado durante buena parte mismo y en el que llegó a dominar por 13 puntos de ventaja, pero que terminó escapándose en un último cuarto, en el que el conjunto italiano impuso su ritmo y castigó los errores de los locales. El conjunto burgalés arrancó con buenas sensaciones y encontró en la aportación interior de Balsa Koprivica y el acierto de Ziga Samar los argumentos para tomar la iniciativa. Los visitantes respondieron al primer golpe de Jallow con un parcial que les permitió situarse por delante, mientras DJ Steward comenzaba a asumir protagonismo ofensivo. El Tortona intentó mantenerse a rebufo gracias a Jallow y Gorham, pero el San Pablo cerró el primer cuarto con una renta favorable de siete puntos (18-25). La dinámica se mantuvo durante buena parte del segundo periodo.y los burgaleses encontraron soluciones para frenar los intentos de reacción locales y volvieron a ampliar su ventaja con la dirección de Samar y los puntos de Steward y Koprivica que permitieron a los de Porfi Fisac marcharse al descanso con una renta de nueve puntos (36-45). Tras el paso por vestuarios, el partido cambió de tendencia y el Derthona Tortona elevó su intensidad y encontró en Hubb una referencia para iniciar la remontada. Los locales fueron recortando distancias hasta poner en peligro la ventaja burgalesa, que llegó a verse reducida a dos puntos y aunque el San Pablo trató de recuperar el control con la aportación de Steward y Samar, el conjunto italiano mantuvo la presión y llegó al último cuarto con el encuentro completamente abierto (58-62). En el periodo definitivo, el Tortona terminó de darle la vuelta al marcador. Alibegovic y Bortolani lideraron el empuje local y permitieron a los italianos colocarse por delante, obligando a Porfi Fisac a detener el juego. Steward sostuvo al San Pablo con varias acciones ofensivas de mérito, acompañado por Koprivica, pero los burgaleses no lograron frenar la respuesta rival (89-79). 89 - Baglietto Derthona Tortona (18+18+22+31): Justin Gorham (15), Dominik Olejniczak (8), Dante Maddox (3), Karim Jallow (8), Aljami Durham (6) -cinco inicial- Paul Eboua (3), Prentiss Hubb (16), Andrea Pecchia (0), Amar Alibegovic (12), Edoardo Di Meo (-), Giordano Bortolani (18), Giulio Gazzotti (-). 79 - San Pablo Burgos (25+20+17+17): DJ Steward (22), Ziga Samar (9), Balsa Koprivica (14), Pablo Almazán (1), Sekou Doumbouya (11) - cinco inicial - Chase Audige (9), Dani Díez (3), Rubén Guerrero (4), Dusan Radosavljevic (1), Christian Sengfelder (2), Raúl Lobaco (3) y Joaquín Taboada (0). Árbitros: Joseph Bissang, Christian Theis, Tolga Akkusoglu. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la jornada 4 del Grupo A de Eurocup celebrado en el Nova Atena de Tortona (Italia).

articles.title: Blake Griffin Says Clippers Haven't Honored 'Lob City' Team, Calls Chris Paul Drama 'Disappointing'
articles.summary: Retired NBA star Blake Griffin believes one of the best periods for the Los Angeles Clippers hasn't received its just due from the organization.
articles.body:
Retired NBA star Blake Griffin believes one of the best periods for the Los Angeles Clippers hasn't received its just due from the organization.

"I don't know," he told Front Office Sports' Dan Roberts about the "Lob City" era being properly recognized. "I don't think we've ever been asked to come back or do anything or honor that team."

Griffin went on to argue he, Chris Paul, DeAndre Jordan and others helped to change the identity of the Clippers.

"Having those expectations and not ultimately achieving our goal of a championship is one thing, but just raising the bar and that cliché of just leaving a place better than you found it [is another]," he said.

The six-time All-Star also expressed his disappointment with Chris Paul's ill-fated return to Los Angeles last season. Paul only made 16 appearances before getting excommunicated .

"Obviously knowing that was gonna be his last season, you would think that they knew what they were getting," he told Roberts. "And part of what you're getting when you sign a Chris Paul is his mind. ... I was just kinda confused at where the disconnect was. This is who he's been his whole career. He's a leader, he's a talker, so why not use that to your advantage?"

The Clippers failed to advance past the second round in any of their playoff trips from 2011-17. However, focusing solely on that doesn't do justice to the what the "Lob City" era achieved.

For the first time since moving to L.A., the team was not only a consistent winner but also fun to watch on a nightly basis. Those are two things that were rarely associated with Clippers basketball.

Does Steve Ballmer still buy the Clippers in 2014 without "Lob City" being in full flight? Signing Kawhi Leonard in 2019 won't be remembered fondly in light of recent events , but that's another big symbolic moment that likely doesn't happen without a proof of concept that the Clippers could contend.

Winning championships is the ultimate objective in sports, but it's not the only thing. Sometimes, it's simply about creating moments, and that happened in spades for Los Angeles in the 2010s.

Griffin isn't wrong for thinking that's worth celebrating.

articles.title: El Valencia Basket patina y sigue sin conocer la victoria (63-77)
articles.standfirst: Las francesas del Carolo Flammes amargan el regreso de Raquel Carrera al Roig Arena
articles.summary: Las francesas del Carolo Flammes amargan el regreso de Raquel Carrera al Roig Arena
articles.body: El Valencia Basket sufrió este miércoles su segunda derrota en la Euroliga ante el Flammes Carolo Basket en un partido en el que siempre fue a remolque del conjunto francés liderado por la base Coline Franchelin con 16 puntos y 9 asistencias y aprovechó su superioridad y su acierto y castigó las 21 pérdidas del equipo valenciano. La noticia positiva para el Valencia Basket fue el regreso de Raquel Carrera, que disputó sus primeros minutos de la temporada tras participar en la WNBA y fue la mejor de su equipo con 10 puntos y 6 rebotes. Después de un inicio marcado por los errores y la precipitación, la inspiración de Leticia Romero por el lado 'taronja' y de Noemie Brochant por el francés animó el partido. El intercambio de canastas y la igualdad se imponían en un Roig Arena que tenía en el regreso de la interior Raquel Carrera la principal noticia. Carrera dejó rápidamente su impronta con 4 puntos seguidos y una asistencia que ponían una pequeña distancia que obligaba al técnico visitante, Romuald Yernaux, a pedir tiempo muerto (16-12, min.7). A pesar de que el Valencia Basket mantuvo su acierto y aumentó su ventaja con un triple de Alexis Peterson, el Carolo Basket había encontrado el camino a base de triples. El acierto de Franchelin, con dos triples seguidos, apretó un marcador que volvió a estar empatado con otro lanzamiento de tres puntos, esta vez de Maia Hirsch (23-23, min.10). La tónica se mantendría en el segundo parcial. Romero y María Araújo lanzaban al Valencia Basket a base de triples, pero el Carolo se reenganchaba para volver a empatar. En un contexto de pocos puntos, quien tuviera la opción de correr encontraría la oportunidad de sumar y ese iba a ser el Carolo. El equipo francés castigaba el balance defensivo del Valencia Basket y aprovechaba las pérdidas para jugar rápido y anotar con comodidad. El Valencia Basket trató de dar un paso adelante y a base de rebotes ofensivos empezó a encontrar canastas con mayor facilidad, pero cada acción era respondida por el Carolo. Incluso la suerte jugó del lado francés con un triple a tablero de Brochant. Y aunque Helena Pueyo anotó un lanzamiento lejano que parecía iniciar un cambio de dinámica, el Carolo no iba a bajar el ritmo y llegó a poner una distancia de 9 puntos. De nuevo Pueyo castigó desde la esquina en otro momento que intentaba aprovechar el Valencia Basket, pero una vez más las pérdidas y el acierto rival con un triple al contraataque, esta vez de Strunc, actualizó la máxima distancia de cara al último cuarto (49-60, min.30). Aún así, llegó a bajar de 10 puntos la diferencia con las canastas de Marta Suárez y de Alisia Jenkins en la pintura. articles.title: Kristaps Porziņģis Trade Packages and Landing Spots Amid Golden State Warriors Trade Rumors
articles.summary: The NBA world got some unfortunate news on Wednesday, when ESPN's Shams Charania posted an update on Kristaps Porziņģis.
articles.body:
The NBA world got some unfortunate news on Wednesday, when ESPN's Shams Charania posted an update on Kristaps Porziņģis.

Charania didn't say it outright, but "seriously contemplating his future in basketball" makes it sound like the Golden State Warriors big man is considering retirement.

That narrows the trade possibilities, even though his contract seems almost designed to be moved.

"Porziņģis is on a trade-flexible contract for $20 million this season and a small partial next year, serving as essentially an expiring deal that the Warriors can utilize, potentially with their pool of assets," Charania added . "He first revealed his POTS diagnosis last year and has had ups and downs with the issue. If there is no breakthrough in recovery, stepping away from basketball -- for good -- is possible."

Before he makes that decision, one way or the other, Golden State looks poised to try to turn his 2026-27 salary into a player who can actually help this season. And some teams could justify taking on an essentially expiring contract attached to a player who won't play.

Of course, Golden State will have to sweeten any potential deals, but they have some assets to do exactly that.

These are the potential trades that make the most sense.

Clippers Receive: Kristaps Porziņģis and a lottery-protected 2032 first-round pick

Warriors Receive: Rui Hachimura (eligible to be traded on December 15) and Jordan Miller

After the league stripped the Los Angeles Clippers of five future first-round picks for circumventing the salary cap, the organization has to be desperate to add whatever draft assets it can.

That means just about anyone outside Keaton Wagler should be available for the right price.

This deal represents exactly that, even if Rui Hachimura and Jordan Miller could both be consistent role players for L.A. this season. Neither will help the Clippers seriously contend, so turning them into a future pick (even a protected one) would be worth it.

For Golden State, surrendering picks that'll convey after Stephen Curry retires is risky, but he's earned a little organizational aggression. And if Butler comes back this season, Hachimura and Miller are both capable of helping the Warriors make a play-in push.

Hachimura, specifically, could be put to good use by an organization that should know how best to deploy his shooting on one end and his defensive versatility on the other.

Kings Receive: Draymond Green, Kristaps Porziņģis, a top-four protected 2032 first-round pick and a 2032 second-round pick

This is a bigger swing, and it comes with a significant sentimental concession.

The front office may not have the stomach to trade a franchise legend, but it may be unavoidable if the Warriors want to get better right now. And while Domantas Sabonis is a clear defensive downgrade, he'd more than make up for that on the other end as a comparable passer to Draymond Green (though maybe not as good a playmaker) and a much more dangerous scoring option. Sabonis is also a better rebounder.

This season, Sabonis' low-post game would make him a good fit with Curry, too. The guard would make it tough for opposing teams to double the big man inside. And he could draw defensive attention inside the three-point line.

As for the Sacramento Kings, they're obviously not going anywhere near serious contention soon. If they can get good longterm assets for either Sabonis or Zach LaVine (and a 2032 pick from the post-Curry Warriors is a great one), they should probably jump on it.

Bucks Receive: Kristaps Porziņģis and a 2032 first-round pick

Warriors Receive: AJ Green and Jaime Jaquez Jr.

The Milwaukee Bucks are another team firmly in asset-accumulation mode. And while 25-year-old Jaime Jaquez could probably fit in this phase, it'd be hard for Milwaukee to pass up a valuable first-round pick for him.

He'll likely be off the roster before the Bucks are ready to seriously contend for titles again, anyway.

He and AJ Green, together, would be worth the steep price for the Warriors. The latter's shooting would instantly be put to good use by Golden State's coaching staff. And though Jaquez's outside shooting leaves something to be desired, his playmaking and feel for the game would make him a good fit in a read-and-react system.

articles.title: Longtime Cincinnati and West Virginia men's basketball coach Bob Huggins dealing with 'progressive cognitive condition'
articles.summary: Huggins won nearly 400 games at Cincinnati and almost 350 games at West Virginia.
articles.body:
Cincinnati and the family of longtime men's basketball coach Bob Huggins announced Wednesday that Huggins is "living with a progressive cognitive condition."

The statement did not say what Huggins was specifically dealing with, but that it has "begun to affect his memory and aspects of his daily life." Huggins is set to be inducted into the Cincinnati Athletics Hall of Fame on Friday ahead of the football team's game against Texas Tech the next day.

Huggins, 73, was the head coach at Cincinnati from 1989 through 2005. The program rose to prominence during his tenure and broke a 14-year NCAA tournament drought when it advanced to the 1992 Final Four.

The Bearcats ascended to No. 1 in the AP Top 25 during the 1996-97 season before finishing at No. 10 following a second-round NCAA tournament loss. In 1999, Cincinnati was the preseason No. 1 team in the AP poll, but lost in the second round again. It was the Bearcats' fourth straight exit in the second round as a No. 2 or No. 3 seed.

Huggins resigned in the spring of 2005 following his DUI arrest a year before and friction with the school's president.

After spending a season out of coaching, Huggins was hired as Kansas State's head coach for a season before leaving to take the head coaching job at West Virginia, his alma mater.

Huggins spent 16 seasons with the Mountaineers before resigning and retiring in June of 2023 following a second DUI arrest. Weeks after his arrest, Huggins had his attorney send a letter to West Virginia saying he had never signed a formal resignation letter to the school.

That arrest also came roughly a month after Huggins had been suspended for the first three games of the 2023-24 season and had his salary reduced for using a slur in a radio interview.

Before coaching at Cincinnati, Huggins was the head coach at Akron for five seasons. He has a career record of 863-389, as 398 of those wins came with the Bearcats and 345 victories came over his time at West Virginia.

When accounting for wins across all NCAA and NAIA divisions — Huggins started his career at Division II Walsh University — Huggins' 935 career wins rank eighth all time among men's coaches.

articles.title: Una segunda parte de récord lanza a La Laguna Tenerife (94-104)
articles.standfirst: Los canarios, liderados por Kyle Guy (26 puntos y 30 de valoración), meten 43 puntos en el tercer cuarto, récord en la historia de la Eurocup, e igualan el tope en una mitad (73)
articles.summary: Los canarios, liderados por Kyle Guy (26 puntos y 30 de valoración), meten 43 puntos en el tercer cuarto, récord en la historia de la Eurocup, e igualan el tope en una mitad (73)
articles.body: La Laguna Tenerife firma unos históricos 73 puntos en el segundo tiempo para imponerse por 94-104 al Skyliners Fráncfort tras un difícil comienzo en el que los de Jaka Lakovic se fueron al descanso 12 puntos abajo en el marcador. Descafeinado inicio de La Laguna Tenerife a domicilio en la cuarta jornada de la Eurocopa, en la que desde el inicio los protagonistas principales de ambos conjuntos dijeron presente. Inició la cuenta Judah Mintz con un triple que fue respondido por otro de Kyle Guy en el primer minuto de juego, que alargó hasta el 5-6 con otro de tres. Dato importante que contrasta con el desenlace del primer tiempo de los aurinegros. Tras el doble acierto de Guy desde el triple, los locales demostraron nuevamente que el duro golpe recibido en la jornada inaugural ante Umana Reyer Venice (104-72), les sirvió para despertar y cambiar el ritmo de juego, al instalar una diferencia creciente en el marcador sobre los isleños que terminó siendo considerable al descanso. El gran lastre de los de Lakovic fue el acierto en el tiro, que fue considerablemente bajo, tras un 38% de transformación en tiros de dos y un 22 % desde el triple al descanso, lo que condenó a los visitantes a irse a vestuarios en una diferencia de 12 puntos que inquietaba visiblemente a los jugadores canaristas, que con sus gestos ejemplificaban cómo no se explicaban la primera parte que habían firmado en el Suwag Energie Arena. Vince Hunter volvió a surgir para el rescate de los isleños en la segunda parte, con 21 puntos y una influencia determinante en ambos aros, que ayudó nuevamente a los suyos a base de ímpetu a reengancharse en el partido y demostrar que La Laguna Tenerife tiene equipo como para competir seriamente en la competición continental. Eñ Skyliners Fráncfort comenzó a notar el arreón visitante y a pesar de un gran Judah Mintz, que acabó con 20 puntos, la producción ofensiva de los alemanes se vio ligeramente afectada, ya que, aún habiendo anotado más puntos por cuarto, los de Perwas no aprovecharon los ataques más seguidos que dio el juego gracias a las rápidas transiciones de un La Laguna Tenerife que activó el modo apisonadora para los segundos 20 minutos. En los primeros 5 minutos del tercer cuarto, los aurinegros ya llevaban los mismos triples que materializaron en los dos primeros y esto fue un pequeño adelanto de lo que vendría a continuación, con un festival de triples especialmente de Guy, Abromaitis y Van Beck. En estos compases de partido se vivió lo totalmente opuesto a los visto en el inicio, en el que La Laguna Tenerife había llegado a estar con una máxima de 15 abajo frente a Skyliners y en esta ocasión, duplicaron esfuerzos para no parar de anotar y remontar el encuentro hasta el punto de colocar el 78-92 en el contador, en apenas seis minutos de juego en el tercer tiempo. Tras cerrar un contundente parcial global de 23-43, los aurinegros no quisieron dar el partido por finalizado y salieron con todo para volver a sellar un abultado cuarto con 30 puntos anotados, en los que destacó nuevamente la decisión de Lakovic de colocar a "los pequeños" para darle una marcha más al juego ofensivo del equipo, que se compaginaron con Shermadini y Vince Hunter para lapidar el partido. Otra gran victoria de La Laguna Tenerife que le sirve para colocarse como líder del Grupo B de la Eurocopa y enlazar cuatro victorias consecutivas, dos en el campeonato continental y alargar la buena racha que han protagonizado en este arranque de curso 26/27 con seis victorias en los primeros ocho partidos de la temporada. 94 - Skyliners Fráncfort (22+21+23+28): Edoka (0), Caisin (7), Christmas (2), Pape (14), Thompson (12) -inicial-, Swope (15), Alleyne (7), Mintz (20), Klepeisz (5), Knauf (2), Bedime (6), Arcidiacono (4). 104 - La Laguna Tenerife (14+17+43+30): Abromaitis (13), TJ Bamba (0), Fitipaldo (3), Guy (26), Happ (5) -inicial-, Fernández (10), Van Beck (13), Huertas (7), Shermadini (5), Hunter (21), Doornekamp (1), Kurucs (0). articles.title: Bob Huggins Has 'Progressive Cognitive Condition,' Family Says Ahead of Cincinnati HOF Induction
articles.summary: The family of college basketball coaching legend Bob Huggins announced Wednesday he's "living with a progressive cognitive condition that has begun to affect his memory, and aspects of his daily life."
articles.body:
The family of college basketball coaching legend Bob Huggins announced Wednesday he's "living with a progressive cognitive condition that has begun to affect his memory, and aspects of his daily life."

The Huggins family released a statement through the University of Cincinnati (via Nick Kosko of On3) outlining his situation:

"While the family has chosen to keep this matter private over the past several months, they believe this is an appropriate time to share the news with the many people who have supported Bob throughout his remarkable career, particularly as he prepares to be honored with induction into the University of Cincinnati's James P. Kelly Athletics Hall of Fame."

Cincinnati called Huggins "undoubtedly one of the greatest coaches in college basketball history."

"He restored Cincinnati basketball to national prominence, ignited a passion for the Bearcats throughout our city and left an indelible mark on generations of student-athletes," the school said.

Huggins, 73, began his coaching career as an assistant at West Virginia in 1977. He got his first Division I head coaching job at Akron in 1984 and spent five seasons there before taking the Cincinnati job.

During his 16 years with the Bearcats, Huggins had a .757 winning percentage and made the NCAA tournament on 14 occasions. They advanced to the 1992 Final Four and the Elite Eight in 1993 and 1996.

After coaching Kansas State in 2006-07, Huggins returned to his alma mater. Building on what predecessor John Beilein established, he made the Mountaineers a tourney mainstay. In 2010, they reached the national semifinals for the first time in more than 50 years.

Huggins retired from coaching following the 2022-23 season. His 863 wins rank 10th in men's Division I history.

The West Virginia native was inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame in 2022.

articles.title: Porzingis medita la retirada por sus constantes problemas de salud y los Warriors estudian traspasarle
articles.standfirst: El pívot letón, que sufre un trastorno que le provoca agotamiento, se ha perdido más de la mitad de los partidos de las últimas tres temporadas
articles.summary: El pívot letón, que sufre un trastorno que le provoca agotamiento, se ha perdido más de la mitad de los partidos de las últimas tres temporadas
articles.body: Los problemas de salud que sufre Kristaps Porzingis desde hace tres temporadas le están haciendo sopesar la opción de la retirada del baloncesto a los 31 años. Eso es lo que asegura el periodista Shams Charania. El pívot letón padece un síndrome de taquicardia ortostática postural, un trastorno del sistema nervioso autónomo en el que el cuerpo tiene dificultades para regular adecuadamente la función cardiovascular. La enfermedad que afecta a Porzingis, que tiene las siglas de POTS, provoca un aumento drástico de la frecuencia cardíaca al ponerse de pie, causando fatiga, mareos y palpitaciones. Es la principal razón por la que se ha perdido el 52% de los encuentros, contando play-in y playoffs, en las tres últimas temporadas, en las que ha jugado en los Celtics, los Hawks y los Warriors. "Sin duda ha sido frustrante lidiar con algunos problemas de salud difíciles de identificar, además de las lesiones que he sufrido a lo largo de mi carrera. Todo se ha ido acumulando, pero lo superaremos", escribió el jugador en sus redes sociales la semana pasada. También despejó las elucubraciones sobre si tenía SIDA o era portador del VIH. Golden State le renovó el pasado verano por dos años y 40 millones de dólares, pero ahora estaría pensando en un traspaso. Sólo 3 de los 20 millones de la segunda temporada están garantizados. Los Warriors, guardándose las espaldas, no hicieron un contrato con ingresos al alza para que Porzingis fuera transferible de inmediato y no tener que esperar hasta mediados de diciembre. El problema será encontrar mercado para un jugador que quizás no vuelva a pisar una cancha. Antes del inicio del 'training camp' de los Warriors, Porzingis avisó a la franquicia de que volvía a sufrir los síntomas de la enfermedad que arrastra desde hace tres años y que estaría de baja indefinida. Durante el 'media day', ni el entrenador Steve Kerr ni sus compañeros de equipo supieron explicar la ausencia del pívot, que ha estado fuera de la dinámica del grupo durante dos semanas. Recientemente se reunió con el mánager general Mike Dunleavy y con el jefe de los servicios médicos de los Warriors. Lo que allí se dijo sigue siendo privado. La franquicia sólo dijo que tenía esperanzas de que Porzingis permaneciera cerca del equipo mientras intentaba mejorar su salud. Parece que no ha sido así. El jugador letón se perderá el inicio de la temporada, empezando por el estreno ante los Lakers. Si volverá a una pista de baloncesto es una incógnita casi tan grande como su salud.

articles.title: Stephen Curry Opens Up on LeBron James Picking 76ers, Reveals if He Thought Warriors Had Chance
articles.summary: LeBron James ended up with the Philadelphia 76ers, but there were times this offseason Stephen Curry thought the King was joining him on the Golden State Warriors.
articles.body:
LeBron James ended up with the Philadelphia 76ers, but there were times this offseason Stephen Curry thought the King was joining him on the Golden State Warriors.

"We took some shots at him," Curry said during an interview with ESPN's Marc J. Spears.

When asked if he ever felt that James was coming to Golden State, Curry said, "There were days I did, days I didn't. If this was high up on his list, we would have felt that. Until you hear the final decision, you've got to think you have a shot. I guess a guy like that, when you have the ability to go anywhere you want in the league to find a place that's right for you."

James would have been yet another aging veteran on a Warriors team that has plenty in Curry, Draymond Green, Jimmy Butler and Al Horford, but he would have been quite the headliner.

And the James-Curry pairing would have been one of the most memorable ones in NBA history seeing how they have combined for eight championships and six MVPs as the two defining players of their generation.

It also surely would have worked on the court beyond just the spectacle.

Curry's gravitational pull as arguably the greatest shooter of all-time would have created plenty of space for James to operate, and there is perhaps nobody better suited to take advantage of that space with the combination of basketball IQ, passing, physicality and scoring touch than the King.

While neither may be at their peak at this stage of their career, the duo would have likely carried the Warriors to plenty of wins this season.

Alas, James joined the 76ers instead and has a number of talented teammates surrounding him with Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey, among others.

He is positioned to challenge for another spot in the NBA Finals, while the Warriors will look to challenge for a Western Conference playoff spot with their own group of veterans.

articles.title: Angel Reese Praised By Paige Bueckers After Historic WNBA Finals Performance in Dream's Game 2 Win
articles.summary: Dallas Wings guard Paige Bueckers is happy her friend is finding so much professional success.
articles.body:
Dallas Wings guard Paige Bueckers is happy her friend is finding so much professional success.

It just so happens that her friend is dominating the 2026 WNBA Finals on the league's biggest stage.

"I'm really happy for her," Bueckers told TMZ Sports when discussing Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese's performance in the Finals against the Golden State Valkyries.

"Me and Angel are close friends, we're great competitors, people who just want the best for each other. We've stayed in contact. Just wishing her the best, talking to her, talking basketball, talking hoops, so to see her thrive on the biggest stage, she deserves it. She works for it. Really happy for her."

Reese has been under the national spotlight since she starred at the collegiate level at LSU, and that has led to plenty of attention and scrutiny as she continues to develop her game.

"The crown that she wears is heavy, but she wears it well, and she wears it with pride," Bueckers said of her Team USA teammate. "Just to see how she handles everything with grace, just being unapologetically herself, I admire that, and so it's really great to see her hoopin!"

Reese was certainly hooping during Atlanta's Game 2 win over the Valkyries on Monday.

She helped lead the franchise to its first-ever WNBA Finals victory and made some history in the process by joining Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones as the only players to finish with 30 or more points and 15 or more rebounds in a Finals game.

The three-time All-Star did a little bit of everything on her way to 30 points, 16 rebounds, three assists and two blocks. That she was so effective on defense is anything but surprising seeing how she was this season's Defensive Player of the Year, but she also got out in transition, scored on the blocks and extended her offensive attack to beyond the arc.

The series is tied at one game apiece as a result, but the Dream now have home-court advantage after splitting the first two in Golden State.

And they could end up lifting the trophy if Reese continues to play at such a high level.

articles.title: Vance condemns 'disgraceful' WNBA national anthem walkouts, says players should show more gratitude
articles.summary: Vice President JD Vance was harshly critical of WNBA players skipping the national anthem during this year's finals, calling them "disgraceful."
articles.body: Vice President JD Vance sharply called out WNBA players in the league finals over skipping the national anthem during an interview Wednesday, calling them "disgraceful." Players from both the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries have left the court during the national anthem before the first two games of the WNBA Finals, despite a rule in the league’s own rulebook specifically calling for players to stand and line up during the performance. "I think it's disgraceful," Vance told host Raymond Arroyo on "Arroyo Grande." "I think that you should not express some criticism of a public policy of a given politician by disrespecting the country writ large. I mean, those women who play for the WNBA, think of the public safety, think of the incredible wealth and privilege, the amazing jobs that they have. They have a lot to be grateful to the United States for, and I think that if they had a bit more of a spirit of gratitude, they'd be happier people, and they wouldn't offend so many people as well." Vance also appeared to cite Saint Augustine’s idea of Ordo Amoris, a concept from Catholic thought that Vance cited in 2025 to defend administration deportation policies. NBA STAYS SILENT ON WNBA FINALS TEAMS SKIPPING THE NATIONAL ANTHEM BEFORE GAMES 1 AND 2 "I've gotten some trouble talking about this, but I'll just talk about it again," Vance said. "One of the ways I understand the Catholic understanding is that we have various orders of duty, and you know, our closest and most immediate duty, of course, is to our family and to the people in our immediate circle. But we, of course, owe duties to the entire world. We owe duties to the stranger. But I also think a good and coherent understanding of the Christian self is that you are part of a national community." He added, "Whether you were born in the United States or whether you came here by choice, this is your country. And I think that we're all meant to love it. We're all meant to try to make it the best version of itself. But fundamentally, I think, without love of country, I think that you're going to be a disordered human being." Fox News Digital spoke to veteran GOP strategist Mary Marslender, who argued, like Vance, that the basketball players lack perspective on how great it is to live in the United States. OUTKICK READERS BLAST WNBA PLAYERS FOR HIDING DURING FINALS NATIONAL ANTHEM "The WNBA players are treating a country that has given them extraordinary privileges as if it were an oppressor, while ignoring that American women enjoy rights and opportunities that remain rare or nonexistent for most women elsewhere," she said. "They seem to forget that a league like the WNBA exists and its players can publicly dissent without fear of state reprisal solely because of these rights and opportunities. If these activists hate this country that much, they are free to leave it. The rest of us are done with this disrespect." Fox News Digital reached out to the WNBA, as well as the Women's National Basketball Players Association, and did not receive an immediate reply. OutKick's Dan Zaksheske contributed to this report. articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom Refuses to Sit in Luxury Suite of State Farm Arena and Leaves WNBA Finals
articles.summary: ATLANTA (AP) — Enes Kanter Freedom refused to sit in a suite the Atlanta Dream and State Farm Arena arranged for the former NBA player's protection at Wednesday night's Game 3 of the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries and instead left the game.
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Enes Kanter Freedom refused to sit in a suite the Atlanta Dream and State Farm Arena arranged for the former NBA player's protection at Wednesday night's Game 3 of the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries and instead left the game.

Freedom demanded he be allowed to sit in his purchased seat, and for the second time this season didn't make it through a WNBA game. He posted a video at halftime saying he had been thrown out of the arena.

"I just got kicked out of a WNBA game for the second time in a row for supporting WOMEN!" Freedom said on his post. "Let that sink in AMERICA!"

Enes Kanter Freedom Says He Will Attend WNBA Finals Game 3 in Atlanta (AP)

The video posted by Freedom showed him being informed at the entry gate: "If you come in you have to agree to go to the suite."

Freedom responded: "I purchased tickets, right? Just because I purchased tickets, I would like to sit in my seat. That's all I want."

An Atlanta police officer told Freedom: "You're free to go to the city of Atlanta streets. That's another private establishment over there. He's free to go there. He just can't be here."

A State Farm Arena public relations official said Freedom "was offered the suite for his safety and he rejected it."

Before the game, a State Farm Arena statement said Freedom had been offered the suite.

"Enes Kanter Freedom has contacted federal, state and local authorities, the WNBA, the Atlanta Dream and State Farm Arena officials to express concerns about his personal safety during his planned attendance at Game 3 of the WNBA Finals tonight," the statement said. "The safety and security of our guests and team members is our highest priority.

"Following consultations with the WNBA, Dream ownership, State Farm Arena leadership and security officials, we have directed Mr. Freedom to watch tonight's game from a private luxury suite. This arrangement is intended to address his security concerns and help provide a safe and positive experience for him and other guests. The suite will have additional security and will be his designated viewing location for the game. State police have also assigned an officer to Mr. Freedom at his request."

Freedom announced on social media on Monday he planned to attend the game. It was his first WNBA game since late August, when he went to see Chicago host Indiana. He was ejected from the game and banned from the arena for getting into a heated interaction with Sky guard Natasha Cloud.

Freedom said he was motivated to attend the game after learning that Golden State star Gabby Williams said she would support a trans athlete playing in the league.

"As you all know, this all started with an interview featuring Gabby Williams of the Golden State Valkyries, when she said, 'I have no problem with trans athletes playing on my team or against my team,'" Freedom said in his post. "Her words gave me so much hope and motivation to come out as a woman and officially declare for the WNBA draft. I can't wait to watch my favorite player, the woman who inspired me to become who I am today!"

Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, have declared for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women. But a person familiar with the decision told The Associated Press in August they are not eligible . WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert has since made that position public.

On Wednesday, Freedom posted a photo of himself in Atlanta and also posted a copy of a letter from Engelbert in which she said replied to a question from Indiana Rep. Marlin A. Stutzman about the eligibility of transgender athletes to play in the league.

"With respect to your questions regarding eligibility, only women are eligible to play in the WNBA and the individuals you cite in your letter are both men," Engelbert said, referring to Freedom and White.

Freedom replied: "Apparently the WNBA still can't define what a WOMAN is, but they're absolutely certain they know what a MAN is! How convenient!"

articles.title: With Kristaps Porzingis' Warriors future in doubt, what could a trade look like?
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors said Wednesday they aren't expecting Kristaps Porzingis to be around in the "immediate future" and didn't deny their interest in tr...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES - Talent, or availability? This was always the question this summer for general manager Mike Dunleavy . On paper, there was no better open-market option at the center position in free agency than Kristaps Porzingis . Provided, of course, that he would actually be on the court .

"In constructing (the roster), we had to make a decision between talent and availability," Dunleavy said. "And there was no perfect solution, in terms of a combination of the two. And I think we leaned a little bit more towards talent, knowing the team that we have, what we need, and hope that we can get some good luck but also improving some areas medically.

"We are taking on some risks there," Dunleavy acknowledged later. "But I think we value the talent over, maybe, finding guys that were perfectly healthy."

Risk, two months later, has drastically outweighed any reward for Golden State in re-upping with Porzingis, who is being paid a guaranteed $20 million this season . A week ago, the Warriors released a statement saying Porzingis would remain out indefinitely for health reasons but would "be around the team." On the afternoon of Wednesday's season opener, though - following an ESPN report that the Warriors were exploring trade options for Porzingis - the club released another statement saying they're now "not expecting Kristaps (to be) around the team in the immediate future."

Porzingis wrote in a tweet , timed with the Warriors' previous statement Oct. 14, that he was dealing with health issues he "can't exactly pinpoint." Golden State was expecting him back in the building more last week. He wasn't. Porzingis' future at large with the Warriors, now, looks murky at best.

"Other than my concern for him and his own well-being, I don't think of it," head coach Steve Kerr said Monday. "When we come to practice, I don't think of it. Because I have to focus on the guys who are here, and that's my concern when we come into the building."

The Warriors said in Wednesday's statement, too, that they "are not going to comment on trade speculation or reports regarding his health-related matter or future." A key element of such statement: The club, clearly, didn't actively deny such trade speculation. And Golden State may be forced to pivot and look for center help, with Porzingis out indefinitely and reserve big Charles Bassey out for Wednesday's opener with knee tendinitis.

The question, though: What could the Warriors actually make happen to move off Porzingis? And what franchise, if any, would see value in a 31-year-old big whose health issues have largely confounded in the NBA?

"I just think the injury concerns, and how bizarre this situation was - I mean, they just signed him," one NBA front-office source told the Chronicle, speaking on condition of anonymity. "They just re-signed him. And now you're trying to trade him? Like, what happened these last couple months? I think there would be too many question marks to justify."

The external value in a Porzingis deal would come from his contract, which the Warriors essentially structured as a one-year flier. Porzingis is only guaranteed $3 million of his $20 million salary for 2027-28 , and could be cut before the full guarantees kick in July 7, according to Spotrac. Organizations looking to move off a player on a longer-term deal could be interested in Porzingis in a one-and-done, salary-match trade. Such is the value of expiring deals in the NBA, for teams that want to create cap room in the future.

Moving Porzingis, though, would be complicated for the Warriors. Golden State is over the first apron, meaning - under the collective bargaining agreement - they couldn't input more salary on a trade than they'd give up. Therefore, they could only take on deals worth $20 million or less this season in shipping out Porzingis.

"That's a little bit of a challenge, right now," as ESPN front-office expert and former NBA assistant GM Bobby Marks told the Chronicle.

There are few obvious targets floating on the market at that number, for teams who'd be actively looking to shed future salary. Orlando's Wendell Carter Jr. might fit the bill - on a three-year deal worth $58 million - but he's currently a starter for a team with playoff expectations in the Eastern Conference.

The silver lining for Golden State: It's sitting just under the second apron, meaning it can aggregate salaries to match incoming value. The most obvious target, then? Milwaukee's Myles Turner, a floor-spacing big who long has been linked with the Warriors and has three years remaining (the final a player option) on a four-year, $108.9 million deal that the Bucks would no doubt desperately love to shed.

To make that work, though, Golden State would have to attach Moses Moody , who's rehabbing a ruptured patellar tendon but a young player the organization loves . And taking on Turner's deal would significantly shrink the Warriors' financial flexibility for the future, solely to input a 30-year-old center with 11 years of NBA mileage on his tires.

There isn't much of an option to simply dump Porzingis and start over. If they cut Porzingis, they wouldn't even have the necessary cap space to sign a free agent to a veteran-minimum deal.

The best - and perhaps only - course of action for Golden State, then? Wait, see if Porzingis suddenly improves, and see how the early season market develops.

"You're going to play this out for a little bit here," Marks said. "I just think that's kinda where - there's no deadline looming, right? So, there's not a sense of urgency."

The Warriors put themselves, in many ways, in this situation. And there are no quick fixes to wriggle out of it.

articles.title: Warriors make their stance clear amid growing Kristaps Porzingis drama
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis warms up before an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Friday, April 10, 2026, in Sacramento, C...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors have yet to tip off the 2026-2027 season against the Los Angeles Lakers on for its season opener, and it's already been an eventful day for them.

Two hours after the report was released, the Warriors addressed the rumors by releasing a statement.

On Monday, head coach Steve Kerr told reporters that he wasn't planning on having the former NBA Champion and All-Star travel with the team this season because he wanted to give him space so that he could focus on the rest of the team.

Porzingis went on to write that he's been getting "better and better" and said he has to stay patient.

In the ESPN report, insider Shams Charania was told by a source that if his health doesn't improve, "stepping away from basketball — for good — is possible for him."

It continues to remain unknown what mystery illness Porzingis is dealing with.

articles.title: Paul George Fined by NBA for Flopping After Celtics' Loss vs. Pistons, 1st of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: Paul George had an excellent Boston Celtics debut, but it was also a costly one.
articles.body:
Paul George had an excellent Boston Celtics debut, but it was also a costly one.

The NBA announced Wednesday he was given a $2,000 fine for flopping during Tuesday's 121-113 loss to the Detroit Pistons. The fine came following a review from the league office and is the first flopping fine assessed for the 2026-27 season.

A fine and a loss surely isn't how George wanted to start his tenure with the Celtics after he arrived this offseason via the trade that sent Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers.

However, he was excellent from an individual standpoint and finished with a franchise record for points in a debut with 38. He also added five steals, five rebounds and three assists while turning back the clock and playing like the peak version of himself from earlier in his career.

"Getting back into the swing of things. Playing again. I thought, really, the camp, legs were just heavy," he told reporters after the showing. "I was winded a lot of times, so it was taking away the ability to kind of do things when I just felt a little heavy and sluggish. But I'm getting my wind back. I'm getting my legs back. I feel like I'm getting my pop back, and so that was kind of the difference maker."

Yet it wasn't enough to prevent Boston from blowing a 22-point lead in large part because it allowed a 23-0 run in the fourth quarter.

Cade Cunningham spearheaded Detroit's comeback with 22 points, eight assists and four rebounds, but it was Ausar Thompson's defense on Jayson Tatum that may have made the biggest difference.

Tatum was an ugly 6-of-23 from the field and 0-of-7 from deep and was unable to match George's impact for the visitors.

articles.title: Enes Freedom leaves WNBA Finals after sparring with police over seating change amid security concerns
articles.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom was directed to watch WNBA Finals Game 3 from a private suite at State Farm Arena but vowed to sit in his purchased seats.
articles.body: Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was seen leaving State Farm Arena on Wednesday after a heated and lengthy confrontation with police at the security entrance over his seating arrangement for Game 3 of the WNBA Finals. Prior to the game, Freedom was directed to watch Wednesday night’s WNBA Finals game from a private luxury suite with additional security after contacting authorities and basketball officials about concerns for his safety. Freedom was seen saying "I guess they'll have to drag me," in a video of a phone conversation with arena security, defying the directive. When he arrived at the arena, he was told that if he were let in, he was told by a security officer he would have to go to the suite that was designated for him, to which Freedom aggressively protested, as seen in footage posted by Benny Johnson. Freedom repeatedly demanded access to the seats he said he had purchased, rejecting the suite arrangement. "I purchased thousands of dollars of tickets, right? And I would like to sit on my seat. That’s all I want," he said. An official cited both Freedom’s previously expressed safety concerns and his ejection from an earlier WNBA game as reasons for the arrangement. "For one, you expressed you were concerned about your security. You showed up here, right, with security," the official said. "So we’re saying we’re gonna make this a safe environment for you." The exchange grew more contentious when an official referenced Freedom’s social media post about a player. Freedom defended the post as free speech. When told he was targeting people, he repeatedly demanded to know whom the official meant. "Give me a name. Give me exactly a name," he said. Freedom was also told he would receive a refund, but continued to reject the arrangement. "I don’t want a refund. I would like to sit on my seat and enjoy the game," he said. He accused those handling the encounter of bullying him and compared the proposed suite restriction to being placed in a cage. Officers ultimately told Freedom he had to leave the property, explaining that he could go onto public streets. He eventually departed, saying, "Well, I guess you got to escort me," before walking away. Afterward, Freedom accused the organizations involved of excluding him because of his advocacy. "They kicked me out of the game for supporting women," he said in a conversation with Johnson. "Shame on the NBA and shame on the WNBA." He also denied having security concerns, despite his earlier statements about threats and the explanation given during the encounter. Asked whether he felt discriminated against, Freedom responded, "Of course, this is discrimination." The arrangement for Game 3 between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries at State Farm Arena follows Freedom’s public claims that he received death threats over his planned attendance. He previously told OutKick he was in contact with the FBI and Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp's office about the threats. State Farm Arena provided a statement to OutKick outlining the security arrangements. The representative responded, telling Freedom, "The only thing available to you tonight is the suite." The number of threats he described has not been independently verified. "My DMs are full of pictures and videos of the moment that Charlie Kirk got shot," Freedom said, adding that the messages warned he would suffer the same fate. He also posted a compilation Tuesday showing messages he presented as threats against him. Freedom said he had contacted the FBI and arranged his own security. A spokesperson for Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp separately told OutKick that the governor’s office had connected Freedom’s team with the appropriate law enforcement resources. Asked how he would respond if a player confronted him, he said he would avoid escalating the encounter and would remain off the court. articles.title: Stephen Curry Reveals He Spoke to Kobe, Tom Brady, Dirk Nowitzki About Legacies, Longevity, More
articles.summary: Stephen Curry is on the short list of the best athletes of all-time across any sport, and the 38-year-old has reflected on his legacy going into what will be his 18th season in the NBA with one organization.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry is on the short list of the best athletes of all-time across any sport, and the 38-year-old has reflected on his legacy going into what will be his 18th season in the NBA with one organization.

And the Golden State Warriors star talked with other NBA legends such as Kobe Bryant and Dirk Nowitzki who were also known for remaining with one team throughout their career, even if those discussions were about more than just franchise loyalty.

"Not specifically about that short list of guys who played for one team. But I talked to Kobe years back, like the year after he retired," Curry told Marc J. Spears of Andscape. "And it was more about the transition into exerting that creative energy into something else. Talked to Dirk, who still lives in Dallas, represents the organization, gets to come back. That connection as a player and now like the ambassador, whatever role he's playing in the organization, how much he's fulfilled by that.

"I've talked to Tom Brady just about longevity and playing. But I think the biggest thing is that there's a mutual respect of all of us of knowing what it takes to carry the torch at that stage and that level for as long as we've been able to do it. And I feel that every single day."

While Brady also played for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers later in his career, he is best known for his 20 seasons as a franchise icon with the New England Patriots.

Brady played until his age-45 season and remained at a high level throughout his career. That is something Curry, who was an All-Star last season and finished in the top 10 of MVP voting in 2024-25, can certainly relate to even if he is past the peak of his career.

As for Bryant and Nowitzki, they remained with the Los Angeles Lakers and Dallas Mavericks for the entirety of their respective careers and were beloved by fans even when they were on the doorstep of retirement.

"To represent the organization for that long, to play in front of one fanbase, and grow up through all the ups and downs, triumphs, the losses, the kind of personal development journey I've been on, and all that … there's definitely a sense of pride being able to see it through," Curry said. "And now I can just play basketball and enjoy it. And that's what I'm excited about."

Regardless of what happens for the rest of his career, Curry is an all-time great with a resume that includes four championships, two league MVPs, two scoring titles, an NBA Finals MVP, 11 All-NBA selections and 12 All-Star nods.

There aren't many who can relate with what he's accomplished, but he made sure to reach out to some of those who could in Bryant, Brady and Nowitzki.
