When the Terrapins called a team meeting for Wednesday morning, the news had already been broken by multiple outlets that included OutKick, players were seen arriving to the football facility for an explanation from those in charge of moving the program forward. Unfortunately, news like this rarely stays quiet until a team can gather privately. Reporters typically wait outside football facilities to speak with players and gauge their reactions after a head coach is fired. Defensive coordinator Aazaar Abdul-Rahim will be the interim head coach for the remainder of the season. WHICH COLLEGE FOOTBALL COACHES IMPROVED OR TANKED THEIR HOT SEAT STATUS FOUR GAMES INTO THE SEASON? Yes, reporters will stand outside the football facility for player interaction That was the case Wednesday, when two University of Maryland student reporters stood outside the athletic complex hoping to speak with players leaving the facility after learning about Locksley’s dismissal. According to one of the student reporters, SB Nation’s Testudo Times journalist Nolan Rogalski, he and Jude Wilkenfeld believed they were permitted to stand outside the football complex because Maryland is a public university. However, a Maryland staff member reportedly called police on the two student journalists for "suspicious activity." Two officers then arrived at the scene and questioned the reporters about what they were doing outside the facility. "For @testudotimes , @JudeWilkenfeld and I were outside Jones-Hill House trying to get players to comment," Rogalski mentioned on social media. "An athletics staffer took pictures of us, and a police dispatch was called for suspicious activity; a cop and 2 cop cars pulled up, and officers ID’d us and asked us to leave." TCU FOOTBALL PULLS CREDENTIALS FROM LOCAL NEWSPAPER FOR REPORTING ON LOCKER ROOM ASSAULT STORY The students appeared to be doing nothing out of line. They were simply covering a major story unfolding on their campus and attempting to speak with players affected by the coaching change. This time last season, there had already been seven head coaches fired in college football, and every single one of them led to reporters in some capacity trying to gather quotes from athletes who were affected by the news. Somewhere, there was a breakdown in communication on Wednesday following the firing of Locksley. Terrapins release statement on police questioning students Whether the school acted out of spite or genuinely did not know what the two students were doing outside the football complex is up for debate. The University of Maryland Police Department recorded the names of Rogalski and Wilkenfeld but said no report was filed regarding the incident. The school and UMPD released a joint statement Wednesday evening emphasizing that they respect the First Amendment rights of journalists. TCU DOES AN ABOUT-FACE AFTER STRIPPING LOCAL NEWSPAPER'S CREDENTIALS DAYS BEFORE FOOTBALL SEASON The statement also cited heightened security concerns surrounding the football program in recent weeks as the reason police were contacted. "UMPD was contacted today, Oct. 21, 2026, about two individuals who were standing outside of Jones Hill House," the statement noted. "Due to heightened concerns for staff and player safety around the football program in recent weeks, there has been increased security around athletics facilities. A UMPD officer approached the two individuals, learned they were with a campus media organization, recorded student IDs, and no report was taken." "UMPD and Maryland Athletics respect the First Amendment rights of all journalists reporting in public spaces." COLORADO FOOTBALL OPENS PRACTICE TO FANS AND REPORTERS, BUT TREATS IT LIKE A CLASSIFIED PENTAGON BRIEFING The Maryland athletic department has recently been criticized over decisions made regarding press conferences involving the now former head coach Mike Locksley. articles.title: Boston Celtics' Paul George hit with flopping fine after 38-point debut ends in collapse
articles.summary: Paul George's 38-point Boston Celtics debut was marred by a $2,000 NBA flopping fine after a dramatic fourth-quarter dive against the Detroit Pistons.
articles.body: The NBA slapped new Boston Celtics forward Paul George with a meager $2,000 fine for flopping during Tuesday’s 121-113 season-opening loss to the Detroit Pistons, the league announced Wednesday. The penalty stemmed from a fourth-quarter sequence with roughly three minutes remaining in regulation. Pushing the ball in transition, George made contact with Detroit guard Duncan Robinson before dramatically collapsing to the floor in an Oscar-worthy attempt to bait a whistle. On-court officials swallowed their whistles in real time, but the league office retroactively assessed the violation upon postgame video review. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Under NBA regulations, postgame flopping penalties begin at $2,000 on an escalating scale. For a superstar commanding nearly $50 million this season, the fine amounts to little more than loose couch cushion change. Tuesday's physical opener frequently devolved into a four-quarter flop-fest with players repeatedly hitting the deck on contested shots, yet George was somehow the only player singled out to receive an invoice from league officials. The slap on the wrist capped an otherwise strong Celtics debut for the nine-time All-Star, who was putting on an absolute clinic. George poured in 38 points on 12-of-21 shooting from the floor, including 7-of-12 from beyond the arc. He added five rebounds, five steals, and three assists in 31 minutes, breaking the franchise record for points in a Boston debut previously held by Kristaps Porzingis. George's individual performance was ultimately spoiled by Boston's collapse. The Celtics squandered a 22-point advantage, largely undone by a sickening 23-0 Detroit run in the fourth quarter led by Robinson and Cade Cunningham. Because the flopping infraction carries no suspension, George remains fully cleared to suit up Friday when Boston hosts his former team, the Philadelphia 76ers. articles.title: Anthony Davis Shines in Wizards Debut Alongside Trae, Box Score Stats, Highlights in Win vs. Bucks
articles.summary: The Washington Wizards are hoping the duo of Anthony Davis and Trae Young can turn them into a playoff contender this year, and they started the 2026-27 campaign on a good note.
articles.body:
The Washington Wizards are hoping the duo of Anthony Davis and Trae Young can turn them into a playoff contender this year, and they started the 2026-27 campaign on a good note.

With top pick AJ Dybantsa sidelined with an ankle sprain, the Wizards downed the Milwaukee Bucks 128-116. Davis, who was traded to Washington from the Dallas Mavericks last season, had a phenomenal debut, and Young posted a double-double.

Every NBA Team's Top 3 Trade Targets This Season 🎯

It's hard to judge the Wizards fairly against a team like the Bucks, who traded Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Miami Heat this offseason and are beginning a rebuild, but picking up a win in their first game is a positive sign.

While Davis was traded to the Wizards from the Dallas Mavericks ahead of the deadline in February, he missed the second half of the season because of a hand injury, so he was unable to make his debut in Washington.

Davis found himself in trade rumors this offseason, mostly regarding LeBron James' free agency, but the Wizards ultimately decided to keep him in Washington as they look to build a playoff-caliber roster.

Wizards fans haven't seen much of Young, either, since he played just five games in Washington last year while nursing various injuries.

The addition of those two should give Wizards fans plenty to be excited about, and Dybantsa's eventual debut only adds to the hype.

Dybantsa was arguably the best college basketball player in the country as a freshman and was an easy choice to be selected first overall. Washington hopes he can eventually be its franchise player.

While nobody is going to proclaim the Wizards as title contenders this year, they have a roster capable of at least making a run at the play-in, if not earning a top-six seat in the East.

It starts with Davis and Young, but the Wizards also have some solid young pieces in Kyshawn George and Alex Sarr, who will both surely develop even further this year.

Time will tell how much of an impact Dybantsa can make early, but it's hard to imagine he won't be a difference-maker as a rookie.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball opens Timberwolves career with 21 points and 6 assists, plus an outrageously bad missed travel
articles.summary: The ESPN broadcast booth could not believe what it was seeing.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves look like a problem with LaMelo Ball aboard. Especially if he's allowed to take more than four steps with the ball.

After landing the All-Star point guard in one of the offseason's biggest trades, the Timberwolves began their season with a 131-106 win over Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Miami Heat on Wednesday .

Anthony Edwards (45 points) and Antetokounmpo (35) led their respective teams in scoring, but Ball himself had a nice Minnesota debut with 21 points, 6 assists and 2 steals. He also had the play everyone was talking about, but not necessarily for a good reason.

During the second quarter, Ball had an open court in front of him but opted to step back for a 3-pointer. At first glance, it might have looked like a normal shot to some people. It was certainly treated as normal, with no whistle from the officials.

Instant replay, however, revealed the truth: Ball got away with a hilariously obvious travel, so much so that the ESPN broadcast was astounded while watching the play in slow motion.

Color commentator Richard Jefferson began to defend the play, saying, "My older basketball players next to me, they feel like this is a travel. Me, I think this is … " but then he was rendered speechless as he got a better look.

The play was bad enough to draw the attention of Ball's older brother, Lonzo, who called the play as he saw it.

It was ultimately a single, silly moment in an otherwise successful debut for Ball, who spent the first six seasons of his career with the Charlotte Hornets before a surprise blockbuster landed him in Minnesota .

The appeal of adding Ball to the Minnesota core is obvious. Edwards is one of the best players in the NBA. Rudy Gobert is an elite defender and rebounder. The rest of the roster is strong, but a distributor like Ball could elevate every player on a team still trying to break through to the NBA Finals.

Wednesday was a good start, taking on one of the East's contenders and having no trouble turning Antetokounmpo's Miami debut into a loss. The Wolves probably shouldn't expect to get away with a similar shuffle at the perimeter going forward.

articles.title: Giannis' Heat Lose to LaMelo's Wolves in Debuts, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Ant, Bam & More
articles.summary: The Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball era in Minnesota is off to a good start.
articles.body:
The Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball era in Minnesota is off to a good start.

Fueled by a dominant night from Edwards, the Timberwolves downed Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat 131-106 in their season opener on Wednesday as Ball made his debut after being traded by the Charlotte Hornets.

While Ball and Antetokounmpo making their respective debuts with their new teams was the storyline coming into the night, Edwards quickly stole the show in Miami.

Edwards posted 21 points in the first half before finishing the third quarter with 36 to help the Timberwolves take an 18-point lead into the final quarter. His 45 points marked a franchise record for the most points in a season opener.

Ball also had a strong showing in his first game with Minnesota, quickly showing how well he can complement Edwards in the backcourt.

While Antetoukounmpo would've liked to start off his Heat tenure with a win, he still had a great showing in his debut. It wasn't quite enough on a night when his supporting cast didn't give him much.

The Timberwolves acquired Ball, hoping he'd give them enough to compete in a loaded Western Conference, and early on, it's fair to say Minnesota looks like it can contend for a championship.

If Edwards has another MVP-caliber season and continues to get strong support from his teammates, the sky is the limit for this Timberwolves team.

The Heat, meanwhile, clearly have some things to figure out. They can't count on Antetoukounmpo to do everything, so they'll go back to the drawing board to figure out how best to play around him.

articles.title: Angel Reese Makes History as Dream Beat Valkyries in WNBA Finals Game 3, Box Score Stats, Highlights

articles.title: Luka Doncic buys out entire parking lot to give Lakers fans free parking for season opener
articles.summary: Luka Doncic bought out an entire parking lot and offered free bike rides across Los Angeles to welcome Lakers fans ahead of the Warriors opener.
articles.body: The LeBron James era in Los Angeles is officially in the rearview mirror, and Luka Doncic wasted no time introducing himself as the new face of the city. Ahead of Wednesday night's season opener against the Golden State Warriors, the Lakers' superstar made an instant impression on everyday fans before even stepping onto the court. Doncic bought out an entire parking lot outside Crypto.com Arena to give fans free parking and teamed up with Metro Bike Share to hand out free rides across Los Angeles all day long. articles.title: Grizzlies Beat Jazz in Peterson, Boozer NBA Debuts, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Ace, Ty Jerome
articles.summary: Rookies Darryn Peterson and Cameron Boozer were the headliners coming into Wednesday's season opener between the Memphis Grizzlies and Utah Jazz, but Ty Jerome stole the show at FedEx Forum
articles.body:
Rookies Darryn Peterson and Cameron Boozer were the headliners coming into Wednesday's season opener between the Memphis Grizzlies and Utah Jazz, but Ty Jerome stole the show at FedEx Forum

Jerome led the Grizzlies to a 123-103 victory behind a stunning 45 points and 17-of-25 shooting from the field. The long-term futures of both teams will depend on their high-profile rookies, but Wednesday's outcome depended on Jerome's individual brilliance.

There will be better offensive days for both Peterson and Boozer, although the latter impressed on the boards and helped his team start the season 1-0. As for Utah, solid showings from Keyonte George and Lauri Markkanen were not enough to earn a win on the road.

While neither team is expected to realistically compete for a title this season, all eyes were on the rookies. Utah selected Peterson with the No. 2 pick of the 2026 NBA draft, while Memphis followed by taking Boozer at No. 3. Throw in Ace Bailey, who the Jazz took at No. 5 last year, and there was plenty of young talent on the court.

However, it was a slow start for both rookies in the scoring department. Boozer had just four points at halftime and struggled with his shot as Jazz defenders swarmed him and cut off his angles, while Peterson had a bit more luck with seven points at intermission.

To their credit, they both found ways to impact the game in the early going beyond their point total. Peterson facilitated when defenders focused too much attention on him, while Boozer contributed on the glass.

With their rookie rebounding, the Grizzlies built a 13-point halftime lead with Jerome taking over for extended stretches and the combination of Jerami Grant and GG Jackson providing an immediate spark off the bench with their outside shooting.

On Utah's side, it was George's shooting and playmaking that kept the visitors within striking distance.

But remaining within striking distance with Jerome playing like he did was a daunting challenge.

The Virginia product took over for stretches in the second half with a combination of floaters in the lane, three-pointers when defenders gave him too much space and drives to the rim when opportunities presented themselves. He was unstoppable and had the Grizzlies in full control even though he was the only starter in double figures heading into the fourth quarter.

The fourth quarter was largely a formality outside of seeing how many points Jerome would end up with in his memorable performance.

It was just the kind of start to the season the Grizzlies wanted, and now they will look to build some early momentum when they hit the road to face the Golden State Warriors on Friday.

articles.title: Atlanta Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries 97-71 to take 2-1 lead in the WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Angel Reese had 21 points and 12 rebounds during the sold-out matchup. The Dream will host Game 4 on Saturday.
articles.body: ATLANTA — Angel Reese had 21 points and 12 rebounds to help the Atlanta Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries 97-71 on Wednesday night and take a 2-1 lead in the WNBA Finals. Rhyne Howard added 16 points and Naz Hillmon had 15 for the Dream, who host Game 4 on Saturday. It was the second straight strong game for Reese, who had 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2, which the Dream also won for their first victory ever in the finals. With the game tied at 49 in the third quarter, Atlanta scored eight straight, including four by Reese. Golden State got within 59-55 on Tiffany Hayes’ layup, but could get no closer as Atlanta closed the quarter scoring 12 of the final 14 points. Atlanta has dominated the third quarter so far in the series, outscoring Golden State 63-35 combined in the three games. With Atlanta up 17 in the fourth quarter, Jordin Canada overthrew Reese on the break, but she saved the ball by throwing it over her head underneath the basket to Howard, who got fouled. Golden State could never recover. Gabby Williams scored 15 points and Hayes added 14 for the Valkyries. This game was originally scheduled to be played on Thursday at the Gateway Center Arena, where the Dream play most of their home games. The league was able to work with the Atlanta Hawks and State Farm Arena to play the next two games of the championship series there so that they could have a much bigger crowd. Gateway only seats 3,500. State Farm Arena can seat more than 17,000 fans. Wednesday night’s game was sold out, as is Game 4 on Saturday, which will also be played at State Farm Arena. The crowd included many music stars, including Ludacris. Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom said he was going to be at the game. The Atlanta Dream and State Farm Arena offered him a private suite for his protection. He refused to sit in it and was removed from the game. The game got off to a slow start as Atlanta led 9-1 after the first five minutes. Golden State missed its first eight shots before Aminata Gueye scored the first basket for the Valkyries with 4:39 left. They got within 13-10 before Naz Hillmon hit consecutive 3-pointers and then Reese hit one. The Dream led 23-15 after the opening quarter. The hot 3-point shooting continued in the second quarter as Atlanta built its lead to 37-26 midway through the period. Golden State was able to hang around and only trailed 46-40 at the break as the teams combined to shoot 15-for-31 (48%) from behind the arc. That was more made 3-pointers in the first 20 minutes than in either Game 1 or Game 2. Reese had 15 points and WNBA Sixth Woman of the Year Janelle Salaun had 11 for the Valkyries. Games 1 and 2 had huge ratings with the opener on NBC averaging 2.1 million, the most ever to watch a first game of the Finals. Game 2, which was broadcast on USA Network, averaged 1.33 million viewers.

articles.title: Anthony Davis ties Wizards record with 34 points in victorious debut vs. Bucks
articles.summary: Anthony Davis made his Wizards debut 257 days after the trade that landed him in D.C.
articles.body:
It took 257 days after his trade from the Dallas Mavericks, but Anthony Davis has finally made his debut with the Washington Wizards. He looked worth the wait.

The All-NBA big man posted 34 points on 11-of-20 shooting, 12 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 steals in a runaway 128-116 win over the Milwaukee Bucks. It's the first time the 1-0 Wizards have had a winning record since Nov. 28, 2022 .

Davis got off to a hot start and received MVP chants at Capital One Arena by the end of the first quarter.

Those 34 points tied Antawn Jamison in 2004 for the most points in a Wizards debut . It's also the first time someone has begun their Wizards career with at least 30 points and 10 rebounds .

Davis was traded to the Wizards on Feb. 5, ending a tenure with the Dallas Mavericks that might have never had a chance due to the emotions tied to him being the return for the infamous Luka Dončić trade.

The Wizards opted to pick Davis up as a new franchise star alongside Trae Young, with two All-Stars thrown into a young core led by Alex Sarr and Kyshawn George. However, with nothing left to play for when they acquired Davis, Washington sat him for the rest of the season with a hand injury. Young also played only five games as a Wizard before getting shut down.

Young, playing his first minutes alongside his new pick-and-roll partner, posted 20 points on 4-of-13 shooting with 13 assists against 1 turnover.

Washington was playing a Bucks team embarking on its post-Giannis Antetokounmpo era, with new acquisition Tyler Herro pacing the team at 24 points. The Bucks actually led 93-90 at the end of the third quarter, but the Wizards blew them out in the fourth.

By comparison, Davis reached 34 points in only two of his 29 games with the Mavericks.

Notably missing from the proceedings was AJ Dybantsa, the No. 1 overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft. The rookie missed the opener with an ankle injury after rolling his ankle on a shot in preseason .

That likely means the best is yet to come for Washington, which suddenly has two former All-Stars and plenty of high-upside young talent after years in the wilderness.

The other side of Davis' debut is the fact he's in a contract year, the last leg of a three-year, $175 million contract he originally signed with the Los Angeles Lakers. His representatives and the Wizards opted to table contract talks until the start of the season .

Davis is eligible for an extension worth up to four years and $275 million, a sum the Wizards are likely hesitant to give based on Davis' injury history and 33 years of age.

articles.title: 'It Means A Lot,' Emotional Tyrese Haliburton Talks Pacers Return From Achilles Injury in Video
articles.summary: After more than a year away, Tyrese Haliburton made his long-awaited return to the court on Tuesday.
articles.body:
After more than a year away, Tyrese Haliburton made his long-awaited return to the court on Tuesday.

The star point guard, who missed all of the 2025-26 season after suffering a torn Achilles in the NBA Finals in 2025, returned to the hardwood in the Indiana Pacers' season-opening win against the New Orleans Pelicans.

Discussing his return after the game, he was understandably emotional.

"It means a lot to be back out here," Haliburton said.

Haliburton spent the last 16 months rehabbing in preparation for his return, and he said he was just "thankful" to get to play again.

And he put together a solid night in his return, posting 23 points and 12 assists as the Pacers escaped with a 123-120 win.

When Haliburton suffered his devastating injury, the Pacers were going up against the Oklahoma City Thunder in Game 7 of the Finals and were on the brink of winning it all.

Now, he's tasked with getting Indiana back to the top of the basketball world, and he's surely more motivated than ever to win his first championship.

articles.title: Enes Kanter denuncia que le impidieron acceder a las Finales de la WNBA "por apoyar a las mujeres"
articles.standfirst: La administración del pabellón explicó en un comunicado que el exjugador había manifestado inquietudes por su seguridad personal a las autoridades federales
articles.summary: La administración del pabellón explicó en un comunicado que el exjugador había manifestado inquietudes por su seguridad personal a las autoridades federales
articles.body: Enes Kanter Freedom, exjugador con 11 años de experiencia en la NBA, denunció que se le negó el acceso al State Farm Arena de Atlanta pese a que había comprado entrada para el tercer partido de las Finales de la WNBA entre las Atlanta Dream y las Golden State Valkyries, después de rechazar el palco privado que le preparó la administración del pabellón. Freedom publicó vídeos en redes sociales en los que lamentó que no le permitieran ocupar los asientos, a pocos pasos de la pista, que había comprado para el encuentro en el State Farm Arena de Atlanta. "¡Acabo de ser expulsado de un partido de la WNBA por segunda vez consecutiva por apoyar a las Mujeres! Que eso cale hondo, ¡América!", compartió en sus redes sociales. La administración del pabellón explicó en un comunicado que el exjugador había manifestado inquietudes por su seguridad personal a las autoridades federales, estatales y locales, así como a la WNBA, las Dream y los responsables del estadio. "¡Qué vergüenza para WNBA. Supongo que tendrán que escoltarme fuera del edificio!", publicó Kanter en X (Twitter). Tras consultar con la liga, la propiedad del equipo y los encargados de seguridad, los organizadores prepararon un palco privado para que Kanter Freedom viera el partido. Freedom afirmó antes del encuentro que la seguridad le estaba impidiendo acceder a sus asientos y que tendrían que acompañarlo fuera del estadio. En otro vñideo, publicado durante el descanso, se escucha a una persona informarle de que solo podría acceder al estadio si aceptaba dirigirse al palco privado.

articles.standfirst: 21 puntos y 12 rebotes de Angel Reese en el triunfo 97-71 de las Atlanta Dream ante las Golden State Valkyries
articles.summary: 21 puntos y 12 rebotes de Angel Reese en el triunfo 97-71 de las Atlanta Dream ante las Golden State Valkyries
articles.body: Las Atlanta Dream, lideradas por los 21 puntos y 12 rebotes de Angel Reese, derrotaron por 97-71 a las Golden State Valkyries y tomaron ventaja 2-1 en las Finales de la WNBA. El encuentro se disputó en el State Farm Arena, al que las Dream trasladaron el partido para disponer de un mayor aforo y Atlanta dio continuidad a su victoria en el segundo duelo de la serie, después de que las Valkyries ganaran el primero, ambos disputados en San Francisco. Reese convirtió 7 de sus 12 tiros de campo, incluidos los 2 triples que intentó, y sus 5 tiros libres. Añadió 3 asistencias y 3 robos en sus 34 minutos en pista. Rhyne Howard acompañó a Reese con 16 puntos, 4 rebotes, 4 asistencias y 5 robos, mientras que Naz Hillmon aportó 15 puntos, con 3 triples de 5 y un 6 de 10 en tiros de campo. La australiana Isobel Borlase contribuyó desde el banquillo con 12 puntos y 5 rebotes. Jordin Canada terminó con 10 puntos, 6 rebotes y 8 asistencias, y Allisha Gray sumó 8 puntos y 6 asistencias. Atlanta comenzó con fuerza y se hizo con 12 puntos de ventaja en el 35-23, aunque Golden State redujo la desventaja a 6 antes del descanso y llegó a igualar el marcador a 48 al principio del tercer cuarto. Las Dream respondieron con un parcial de 23-9 que les dio ventaja 71-57. Las Valkyries no consiguieron remontar y un 7-0 de Atlanta en el último periodo elevó la diferencia a 20 puntos en el 80-60. El equipo local acabó con 34 de 69 en tiros, un 49,3% de acierto, frente al 34,8% de Golden State, que convirtió 24 de sus 69 lanzamientos. Las Dream repartieron 26 asistencias y solo perdieron 8 balones, por las 19 asistencias y 15 pérdidas de sus rivales. Gabby Williams fue la máxima anotadora de las Valkyries con 15 puntos y añadió 8 asistencias y 3 robos, pero terminó con un 5 de 18 en tiros de campo. Tiffany Hayes aportó 14 puntos desde el banquillo. Cecilia Zandalasini y Janelle Salaun anotaron 13 puntos cada una. La italiana convirtió 4 triples en 6 intentos y la francesa metió 3 de 4. Kiah Stokes capturó 11 rebotes y puso 3 tapones, aunque se quedó en 2 puntos. Veronica Burton terminó con 3 puntos, 4 asistencias y un 1 de 7 en tiros de campo. Atlanta tuvo cinco jugadoras en dobles dígitos y cerró su segunda victoria consecutiva en la serie con una diferencia de 26 puntos que les acerca al anillo.

articles.title: 'It means a lot to be back out here': Tyrese Haliburton tears up after starring late in Pacers' win over Pelicans
articles.summary: Sixteen months after the injury that paused his career, the Pacers' All-Star point guard's return to the floor was an emotional affair.
articles.body:
The moment that Tyrese Haliburton had spent the last 16 months waiting for came on Wednesday night, with his Indiana Pacers coming down to the wire on the road against the New Orleans Pelicans in their first game of the 2026-27 NBA season.

And after everything he'd gone through to get back here — the surgery to repair his ruptured Achilles tendon , the grueling rehab complicated by a nasty case of shingles , day after day of waiting and straining and striving after being laid low just as he reached for the brass ring — Haliburton damn sure wasn't going to let it pass him by.

With the score knotted at 118 and a minute and a half remaining in regulation in New Orleans, Haliburton brought the ball into the frontcourt, took a ball screen from teammate Pascal Siakam, and stared down Pelicans forward Zion Williamson high above the 3-point arc. He crouched, lingered, tensed. He sold Williamson on a right-hand in-and-out dribble before hesitating and crossing back to his left, pushing off that surgically repaired right leg as he created enough space to drive to the middle of the floor.

Haliburton got his shoulders even with the recovering Williamson, absorbed the contact in the lane and leaned left, lofting a floater with his off-hand. It rattled home. The bucket, plus the foul, and as he sat up on the deck at the Smoothie King Center, the All-NBA point guard roared, letting 486 days' worth of pent-up emotion and frustration out for all to see.

The and-1 free-throw gave the Pacers a three-point lead with 1:23 to go. The Pelicans would have two chances to tie the game and force overtime — a top-of-the-key 3-pointer by second-year guard Jeremiah Fears, and a left-corner try by Williamson after an offensive rebound — but neither found the bottom of the net, allowing Indiana to finish off a 123-120 win .

After missing seven of his first 11 field-goal attempts through three quarters, Haliburton came alive in the fourth, scoring 13 points on perfect 4-for-4 shooting in the final frame to help the Pacers come back in a game the Pelicans had largely controlled in the previous two quarters. Time and again, when the Pacers needed a good look, they put the ball in Haliburton's hands, let him run the two-man game with Siakam, and forced the Pelicans to try to hold up and get stops against their All-Star inside-out tandem. They couldn't:

Haliburton finished with 23 points on 8-for-15 shooting to go with 12 assists in 34 minutes of work — his 70th 20-10 game as a Pacer , and his first since Game 3 of the 2025 NBA Finals .

After sealing the win, Haliburton found himself overcome by emotion during his walk-off interview with Pacers sideline reporter Jeremiah Johnson:

"It means a lot to be back out here," Haliburton said, tears streaming down his face as he struggled to find the words.

The Pacers faithful that traveled down to New Orleans to welcome back their leader were all too happy to offer their help:

After heading back to the locker room and taking some time before meeting with reporters, Haliburton took stock of what led to those emotions overflowing on the floor after the final buzzer.

"I don't think there's been a point where I — like, I've had moments in private, especially early, when it was hard," Haliburton said, according to Tony East of Circle City Spin . "You know, I don't know. I just thought that this moment would feel super emotional for me. I didn't think I was going to cry. I really didn't. But I think it all just hit me kind of there when talking to Jeremiah, and seeing all those Pacers fans in the arena. We haven't won here in, what, five years or whatever? And to see all those Pacer fans here in New Orleans for this means a lot to me. This organization, this city means a lot. And it just means a lot for me to be back doing what I love."

Asked what emotion specifically grabbed hold of him, Haliburton thought for a moment before saying, "I think just an appreciation."

"You know, perspective is everything," he said. "And as the game was going on, I was struggling a little bit. I was tired, and just not playing well. We weren't playing well. I think I was kind of sitting there in that moment, and what got me going again was just … like, I've had those moments before, where it's kind of like, 'Oh, I need this game to get done. I need to breathe so I can get to tomorrow, next game, whatever.' And in that moment, I just kind of took a step back when I was on the bench there, and I was like, 'Man, I'm back playing. Like, I'm back here. And I just want to live in the moment as much as I can.'"

articles.title: Takeaways from the Chicago Bulls’ season-opening 135-92 loss, including Caleb Wilson’s messy debut
articles.summary: The NBA never takes long to introduce itself to a newcomer. It doesn’t matter how polished or well-programmed a rookie thinks himself to be in the days and w...
articles.body:
The NBA never takes long to introduce itself to a newcomer.

It doesn't matter how polished or well-programmed a rookie thinks himself to be in the days and weeks before his debut. Blue chip program, AAU glory, top draft pick — nope, none of that matters. It's the NBA. Excellence is pedestrian here.

This is the lesson Chicago Bulls' No. 4 draft pick Caleb Wilson learned the hard way 71 seconds into the first game of his NBA career. Wilson thought he had Kawhi Leonard beat off his initial step. The Toronto Raptors didn't have a low man in position, which meant Wilson had a clear path straight to the rim. All he needed to do was beat Leonard off the dribble.

But that's a bold assumption to make when being guarded by a two-time champion who forged a nickname off the crafty quickness of his hands as a defender. Wilson crossed the ball over at a relaxed pace and Leonard extended one arm to the totality of his 7-foot-3 wingspan to poke it away. By the time Wilson clocked the loss of possession, half the Raptors roster was already down the court.

Many errors and missteps followed that initial turnover in the 135-92 season-opening loss in Toronto. But that opening mistake captured the yawning chasm between where Wilson is right now and where he hopes to be someday.

"Honestly, it was kind of surreal because it's Kawhi — it's The Claw," Wilson said after the loss. "I was just thinking about what I could do to counter that when I was on the way back. … It's just something you learn."

Wilson's first rotation was an assortment of blunders. He missed both of his shots. He lost his handle attempting to push the pace in transition, windmilling his arms haplessly as the ball squibbed backward and into the hands of Immanuel Quickley. He couldn't rebound on defense and let the ball get stuck on the offensive swing.

The game settled down a bit after that first rotation, but Wilson still spent most of his debut playing with the well-meaning gracelessness of a puppy who has yet to grow into his paws. He tripped over his own feet trying to execute a spin move into a double team. He stepped on the sideline while jab-stepping in the corner. He practically jumped into Jakob Poeltl's arms while attempting to navigate a pair of screens on defense.

It wasn't all bad. Wilson played more than 32 minutes. That's too much time for a talented rookie to go without any highlights. But every time Wilson delivered a redemptive move, the Raptors found a way to knock him back down.

The rookie tossed himself into the air at an acute angle to roll in a layup for his first basket of the game. On the ensuing play, Scottie Barnes knocked down a 3-pointer in his face. Wilson recovered a minute later, nailing a 3-pointer. So Quickley countered by trotting up the court and sinking yet another 3 right over the rookie. Wilson rocked the stanchion of the Toronto basket with a ferocious dunk in transition in the fourth quarter, only to have his next attempt at a full-court sprint smacked away by Jamal Shead and silenced with a 3-pointer from Leonard.

The Raptors were, collectively, bigger and faster and meaner. It's the first time the rookie has encountered a court full of players who all had his number in such a fashion. Wilson finished with 16 points, but also coughed up nine turnovers against zero assists. He tallied a team-worst plus-minus ranking of minus-45. It's a performance the rookie isn't trying to repeat any time soon, but it's also not one that he wants to hang around. This was Wilson's first night in the NBA. It was his first time out of the country. The firsts will end eventually. The learning won't.

"I definitely don't beat myself up," Wilson said. "I don't let anybody else's expectations get to my head. Of course, I could have done things better out there, but it's my first NBA game. I can't expect myself to go out there and go for 30. That's not what I'm trying to do. I'm trying to learn, to get better every game and it's going to happen over time."

Here are three more takeaways from the loss.

For those who don't want to flex their arithmetic abilities — the Bulls lost this game by 43 points. That's a worrisome way to start any season, but especially for a team that could not manage more than 92 points even after the Raptors cleared their bench to run down the blowout.

One game in, it is unclear how exactly the Bulls plan to score points this season. This offense does not feature any clear isolation scorers or playmakers. Josh Giddey, the team's primary facilitator, coughed up five turnovers against six assists and struggled to progress the ball past half court. Matas Buzelis and Wilson could not create pathways to the rim. Often, the Bulls fell into a flat-footed stance in the half court, looking around as if waiting for an instruction that would never come.

The most consistent scoring for the Bulls came from veterans Norman Powell , Jalen Smith and Tre Jones. The Bulls had to score more than a third of their points from the free-throw line while doling out a miserable 31.8% from the floor. They went 4-for-36 from behind the arc. Wilson, Powell and rookie Jaylin Sellers provided the only long-range makes of the night.

That isn't enough. Ninety-two points aren't enough, either. The Bulls aren't going to get better at dribbling or breaking down defenders one-on-one overnight, but they can shore up these weaknesses by moving off the ball, cutting into space and passing with intensity. Without those factors, the Bulls will lag behind opponents regardless of their defensive acumen.

The Bulls knew that Wilson — and the rest of the team's rookies — might receive a wake-up call in the first game of their NBA careers. But more concerning for Chicago was the lack of impact from third-year forward Matas Buzelis, who struggled to achieve his goal of pressuring the Raptors at the rim.

Buzelis did try to force the issue, but he managed only eight shots on the night — half of which came from behind the 3-point arc. The forward got stuffed by double-team blocks and turned away by larger Toronto wings, who manhandled the slighter forward in his attempts to create downhill momentum. Buzelis scored 17 points on 25% shooting and played nearly eight fewer minutes than Wilson.

This lack of penetrative ability from Buzelis highlighted a more extensive problem for the Bulls, who have no individual ability to create off the dribble. A step forward from Buzelis would have given the Bulls an offensive outlet. Without that, this offense will only continue to flounder this season.

Wednesday's season opener marked a monumental occasion in Toronto — the return of Kawhi Leonard, the franchise legend who has not played in a Raptors jersey since he won the team a championship in 2019. Leonard, 35, signed a two-year, $115 million deal with the Raptors over the summer to return to the city that made him a champion for a second time.

Raptors fans turned out in droves to celebrate Leonard's return to ScotiaBank Arena, donning white giveaway shirts that featured the star's hand extended in his "claw" signature. But it was also a welcome reunion for Bulls coach Tiago Splitter and veteran guard Norman Powell, both of whom won an NBA championship as Leonard's teammates. Leonard was drafted by the San Antonio Spurs the year after Splitter joined the team and the pair spent four seasons as teammates, including a championship run in 2014. Splitter praised Leonard as a quiet teammate with a loud presence on the court.

"He would just steal my rebounds back in the day," Splitter joked.

Powell won a championship with Leonard in Toronto, but stayed for two more seasons after the team won the chip. His 2022 trade to the Portland Trail Blazers did not sever a strong connection to the Toronto fan base, who welcomed him back warmly. Before the game, Powell noted that Leonard has grown into his star power in the six seasons since they played together.

Leonard did not overwhelm in his first outing back in Toronto, but he still managed 23 points in his return.

articles.title: Angel Reese Drops Epic Quote to Explain Mindset During Dream's WNBA Finals Run
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese posted 21 points, 12 rebounds and three steals to lead her team to a 97-71 home win over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wednesday evening.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese posted 21 points, 12 rebounds and three steals to lead her team to a 97-71 home win over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wednesday evening.

After the game, Reese dropped this quote regarding her mindset this season.

Lindsay Gibbs of CBS Sports asked Reese how she's grown as a leader this year, noting that the team was feeding off her Wednesday. Reese provided this response.

"Just try to show up every day and be consistent for the team," Reese began. "No matter whether my shots are falling, I just want to make sure I bring energy, and hopefully I can stay the same, but every day I just want to come in every day and just pour into everybody, bring the energy, bring the morale, because I think it's contagious.

"When you have a mentality that started from me, where I'm hype all the time, and bringing the confidence into everybody, y'all not taking this from us. And in my heart, I'm not letting you take this from us, and it becomes contagious within the team. They feel that confidence too. So that's kind of been my mindset throughout the entire season, just being able to want it more than anybody else."

Atlanta lost Game 1, 68-64 in a tough defensive battle, but the Dream have since rallied for a pair of big wins. In Game 2, Atlanta won 79-65 thanks in large part to Reese, who posted a monster performance (30 points, 16 rebounds).

The Dream certainly didn't let the Valkyries take Game 3 from them, outscoring the visitors 51-31 in the second half. Reese was fantastic on both ends, notably shooting 7-of-12 (5-of-5 from the free throw line) and helping hold Golden State to 34.7 percent shooting.

Atlanta will look to take a 3-1 series lead on Saturday when it faces Golden State at 1 p.m. ET in State Farm Arena.

articles.title: Damian Lillard's Return, Ja Morant's Debut Key Blazers vs. Suns, Box Score Stats & Highlights
articles.summary: Welcome back, Damian Lillard.
articles.body:
After sitting out the 2025-26 season and playing the previous two campaigns for the Milwaukee Bucks, the Portland Trail Blazers legend's return to the court for the franchise he is most closely associated with couldn't have gone much better during Wednesday's 124-83 victory over the Phoenix Suns.

Lillard looked like his old self while unleashing silky smooth shots from beyond the arc on his way to 25 points. He wasn't the only notable Trail Blazers guard, as Ja Morant provided secondary scoring and timely assists in his first game with the team.

A solid showing from Devin Booker on the other side was nowhere near enough as the Suns started their season with a blowout loss.

The biggest question surrounding the Trail Blazers this season is how the Lillard and Morant pairing will hold up from both a health perspective and basketball fit.

If Wednesday was any indication, Portland has nothing to worry about.

The home team scored the first 21 points of the game in a stunning start and won the first quarter 43-12. The game was essentially over the rest of the way, which allowed the backcourt duo to play freely and avoid seeing too many minutes early in the season.

Morant and Lillard each hit from deep during that initial spurt to seize control and remained willing facilitators whenever defenders collapsed.

There is no question Lillard is going to stretch the floor with his outside shooting, but Morant finding his stroke from deep would be particularly important for Portland. That will clear the lane even more for Deni Avdija to attack in space, which could fully unlock the team's offense.

Avdija was the Trail Blazers' go-to option last season with Lillard sidelined and Morant not even on the team, and he will surely remain a focal point even with the veteran guards handling the ball.

That was clear Wednesday, as he notched a double-double while attacking the rim and even shooting from deep on his own as a matchup nightmare.

There will be more challenging games for the Trail Blazers this season, but everything clicked in the opener.

And now they will look to keep things rolling when they hit the road to face the Sacramento Kings on Friday.

articles.title: El primer recital de Anthony Edwards chafa el estreno de Antetokounmpo con los Heat
articles.standfirst: El escolta de los Wolves mete 45 puntos y se suma a una lista con Wilt Chamberlain y Michael Jordan
articles.summary: El escolta de los Wolves mete 45 puntos y se suma a una lista con Wilt Chamberlain y Michael Jordan
articles.body: El primer recital de la temporada NBA corrió a cargo de Anthony Edwards y sirvió para chafar el debut de Giannis Antetokounmpo con los Heat. El escolta de los Timberwolves anotó 45 puntos con nueve triples y atrapó 10 rebotes para que su equipo se impusiera en Miami por 106-131. El curso pasado ya anotó más de 40 en su estreno, así que se suma a Wilt Chamberlain (cuatro veces) y Michael Jordan (tres) como los únicos que han llegado a esa cifra en varias ocasiones en su carrera en la jornada inaugural. Los aficionados de los Heat se las prometían felices en el inicio de esta nueva era con Antetokounmpo al frente, pero se llevaron un chasco a la primera. El alero griego hizo 35 puntos (21 de ellos antes del descanso) con 13/19 en tiros de campo y añadió seis rebotes. Sin embargo, acabó siendo expulsado por faltas en su primera noche jugando como local en Miami. Los Wolves mandaron desde el segundo cuarto y se dispararon en el marcador con un parcial de 7-23 (61-78) que comandaron entre Edwards y LaMelo Ball, autores de 17 puntos en ese tramo. El base, que hacía su debut con la franquicia de Mineápolis, acabó con 21 puntos y seis asistencias. Mejor que la segunda espada rival, Ban Adebayo, que sumó 15 con siete rebotes. Pese a un tramo de numerosas pérdidas, los Heat consiguieron estar en el partido. Perdían por ocho a mitad del tercer cuarto, pero de nuevo Edwards entró en erupción para meter 18 puntos desde ahí hasta el final y asegurar un cómodo triunfo de unos Wolves que tienen grandes esperanzas depositadas en esta temporada. Los Heat lo intentaron desde el triple, pero fallaron 11 de los últimos 12. El duelo de estrellas fue para 'Ant man' en lo colectivo y en lo individual.

articles.title: Grizzlies rookie Cam Boozer sets new franchise record in NBA debut vs. Jazz
articles.summary: Cam Boozer did not have his shot falling in his NBA debut, but the Memphis Grizzlies rookie still found a way to make history. Boozer finished with seven po...
articles.body:
Cam Boozer did not have his shot falling in his NBA debut, but the Memphis Grizzlies rookie still found a way to make history. Boozer finished with seven points, 11 rebounds and five assists as the Grizzlies routed the Utah Jazz 123-103 in their season opener on Wednesday night at FedEx Forum.

His shooting was rough, as he went just 2-of-15 from the field, but Memphis outscored Utah by 32 points with him on the floor. According to StatMuse , that +32 mark is the highest plus-minus by any player in a season opener in Grizzlies franchise history.

It was a fitting introduction for the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft . Boozer arrived from Duke with a reputation as a polished, do-it-all forward, and even on an off shooting night, he found other ways to help. He knocked down 3-of-4 free throws and made his presence felt on the glass, with Memphis' rebounding helping it build a 13-point halftime lead.

The rookie had only four points at the break, but he kept finding ways to contribute without scoring.

Boozer also benefited from a historic night by a teammate. Ty Jerome exploded for 45 points on 17-of-25 shooting, adding seven rebounds and six assists, and took over in the second half with an array of floaters, three-pointers and drives to the basket. Jerami Grant and GG Jackson also provided outside shooting off the bench.

The night was also a showcase of top rookies. Utah's Darryn Peterson, the No. 2 overall pick, made his debut as well and finished with nine points, four rebounds and three assists. Ace Bailey added 12 points, five rebounds, three assists and three blocks for the Jazz.

Keyonte George led Utah with 22 points and five assists, while Lauri Markkanen chipped in 18 points and nine rebounds, but the Jazz could not keep pace once Jerome got rolling.

For Boozer, the debut offered a glimpse of what Memphis is hoping for . The shots will come, but his rebounding and playmaking were already making an impact.

The Grizzlies will look to keep it going when they visit the Golden State Warriors on Friday.
